title.en: Volume 339 Biographies 126: Heng Wen, Guo Yiyu, Jiang Zhou, Yang Hao, Gao Heng Son: Pu, Wang Danwang, Lei Er Jin, Chen Huizu, Zheng Yuanshuang, Guo Tai, Hao Shuo, Liang Qing, Fang Shijun, Qian Du, Jue Luo Wu La Na, Pu Lin
title.raw: 卷339 列傳一百二十六 恒文 郭一裕 蒋洲 杨灏 高恒子：樸 王亶望 勒尔谨 陈辉祖 郑源鹴 国泰 郝硕 良卿 方世俊 钱度 觉罗伍拉纳 浦霖

sentences.zh: 恆文，烏佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Heng Wen, of the Wujia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Wen, of the Wujia clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain Yellow.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，以諸生授筆帖式，四遷兵科給事中。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongzheng reign, as a licentiate scholar he was appointed a bithesi clerk; after four promotions he became a supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he entered service as a licentiate appointed bithesi clerk, and after four promotions reached supervising secretary in the military bureau.

sentences.zh: 外授甘肅平慶道，再遷貴州布政使。

translations.literal: He was posted outside the capital as intendant of Pingqing Circuit in Gansu, then promoted again to provincial administration commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posted outside the capital as intendant of Pingqing in Gansu, he was later promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，方用兵金川，恆文奏言：「兵貴神速。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianlong reign, when troops were being mobilized against the Jinchuan, Heng Wen memorialized: "In warfare speed is prized.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianlong reign, while the Jinchuan campaign was underway, Heng Wen memorialized: "In war, speed is everything.

sentences.zh: 臣官甘肅平慶道時，見提督以下諸營，或三之一，或四之一，擇勇健者，名為援剿兵將，備預定旗幟器械，及獎賚諸項亦預存。

translations.literal: When I served as intendant of Pingqing in Gansu, I saw that below the provincial commander-in-chief, in each camp either one-third or one-fourth of the men were chosen from the brave and hardy and designated relief troops for suppression; banners, equipment, and reward items were all kept ready in advance.
translations.idiomatic: When I was intendant of Pingqing in Gansu, I saw that in camps under the provincial commander either a third or a fourth of the troops were picked from the sturdiest men and designated as relief forces for suppression; banners, gear, and rewards were all laid in beforehand.

sentences.zh: 貴州乃無此例。

translations.literal: Guizhou had no such precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou had nothing of the kind.

sentences.zh: 本年四川調兵二千，遲至六日方得起程。

translations.literal: This year two thousand troops were transferred from Sichuan, yet six days passed before they could set out.
translations.idiomatic: That year two thousand troops were called up from Sichuan, yet six full days passed before they could march.

sentences.zh: 請仿甘肅例預為計，提督駐安順，設重兵，請於府庫貯銀五千待用。」

translations.literal: I ask that planning follow the Gansu example: with the commander-in-chief stationed at Anshun and heavy forces posted there, five thousand taels be stored in the prefectural treasury against need."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we follow the Gansu model and plan ahead: station the commander-in-chief at Anshun, keep substantial forces there, and set aside five thousand taels in the prefectural treasury for immediate use."

sentences.zh: 既又疏上行軍諸節目。

translations.literal: He also memorialized separately on various matters concerning troop movements.
translations.idiomatic: He later submitted another memorial detailing the particulars of marching troops.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其能治事，移直隸。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his capacity for administration and transferred him to Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended his administrative ability and moved him to Zhili.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢湖北巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor of Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 疏請採漢銅廣鼓鑄，請增築武昌近城石堤，請停估變省城道倉空廒、備貯協濟鄰省米石，均得旨允行。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that Han bronze drums be widely cast, that the stone dike near Wuchang city be reinforced, and that the reassessment and conversion of vacant granaries along the provincial highway and the stockpiling of grain and rice to assist neighboring provinces be halted—all were approved by imperial decree.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to cast more Han-style bronze drums, to raise the stone embankment near Wuchang, and to halt reassessment of empty highway granaries and stockpiling of grain to aid neighboring provinces—all approved.

sentences.zh: 十八年，署湖廣總督，移山西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he acted as governor-general of Huguang, then was transferred as governor of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he served as acting governor-general of Huguang, then was made governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三月，疏劾貴州糧道沈遷婪索屬吏，鞫實論斬。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-second year he memorialized impeaching Shen Qian, grain intendant of Guizhou, for extorting his subordinates; investigation proved the charge and he was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twenty-second year he impeached Shen Qian, Guizhou grain intendant, for extorting subordinates; the case was proved and Shen was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 恆文與雲南巡撫郭一裕議制金爐上貢，恆文令屬吏市金，減其值，吏民怨諮。

translations.literal: Heng Wen and Guo Yiyu, governor of Yunnan, agreed to cast a golden censer as tribute; Heng Wen ordered his subordinates to purchase gold and reduced its price, provoking complaints from officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: Heng Wen and Yunnan governor Guo Yiyu agreed to commission a gold censer as tribute; Heng Wen had subordinates buy the gold at reduced rates, and officials and commoners alike protested.

sentences.zh: 一裕乃疏劾恆文貪污敗檢，列款以上。

translations.literal: Yiyu then memorialized impeaching Heng Wen for corruption and moral ruin, listing charges item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyu then impeached Heng Wen for corruption and debased conduct, setting out the charges in detail.

sentences.zh: 上命刑部尚書劉統勳會貴州巡撫定長即訊，得恆文令屬吏市金減金值，及巡察營伍縱僕婪索諸事，逮送京師。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Minister of Justice Liu Tongxun, together with Guizhou governor Ding Chang, to investigate on the spot; they established that Heng Wen had ordered subordinates to buy gold at reduced value and that while inspecting camps he had allowed servants to extort, and he was arrested and sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Minister of Justice Liu Tongxun and Guizhou governor Ding Chang to investigate at once; they confirmed Heng Wen's gold purchases at deflated prices and his servants' extortion on camp inspections, and had him sent to Beijing.

sentences.zh: 上責恆文；

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Heng Wen:
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked Heng Wen:

sentences.zh: 「為大臣，以進獻為名，私飽己橐，簠簋不飭，負恩罪大。」

translations.literal: "As a grand minister, under the name of presenting tribute you privately filled your own purse; your conduct was corrupt and your ingratitude a grave offense."
translations.idiomatic: "As a senior minister you used tribute as a pretext to line your own pockets; your integrity failed and your ingratitude was a grave crime."

sentences.zh: 遣待衛三泰、扎拉豐阿乘傳就恆文所至，宣諭賜自盡。

translations.literal: He dispatched guardsmen San Tai and Zhala Feng'a by relay to wherever Heng Wen was, announced the decree, and granted him suicide.
translations.idiomatic: He sent guardsmen San Tai and Zhala Feng'a by urgent relay to Heng Wen's location to announce the decree and permit him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 郭一裕，湖北漢陽人。

translations.literal: Guo Yiyu was a native of Hanyang, Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yiyu was from Hanyang in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，入貲為知縣，除江南清河知縣。

translations.literal: Early in the Yongzheng reign he purchased office and became a district magistrate, appointed magistrate of Qinghe in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongzheng he bought his way into office as district magistrate and was appointed to Qinghe in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 稍遷山西太原知府。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to prefect of Taiyuan in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to prefect of Taiyuan in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，累擢雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he was repeatedly promoted until he became governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he rose step by step to governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 恆文對簿，具言貢金爐議發自一裕。

translations.literal: At his trial Heng Wen stated in full that the plan to present the gold censer had originated with Yiyu.
translations.idiomatic: At trial Heng Wen testified that the gold-censer tribute had been Yiyu's idea.

sentences.zh: 統勳等察知一裕亦令屬吏市金，見恆文以減值斂怨，乃先發為掩覆計。

translations.literal: Tongxun and others found that Yiyu too had ordered subordinates to purchase gold; seeing that Heng Wen had drawn resentment by reducing the price, he had struck first as a cover.
translations.idiomatic: Tongxun's inquiry showed Yiyu had also ordered subordinates to buy gold; seeing Heng Wen blamed for cutting prices, Yiyu had impeached him first to cover his own tracks.

sentences.zh: 事聞，上謂：「一裕本庸鄙，前為山東巡撫，嘗請進萬金上供。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor said: "Yiyu was vulgar and base by nature; when he was earlier governor of Shandong he once asked to present ten thousand taels in gold as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, the Emperor said: "Yiyu was coarse and low by nature; as Shandong governor he had once offered ten thousand taels in gold as tribute.

sentences.zh: 在官惟以殖產營運為事，但尚不至如恆文之狼藉。」

translations.literal: In office he cared only for amassing property and business ventures, yet he had not reached Heng Wen's degree of disorder."
translations.idiomatic: In office he thought only of piling up wealth, yet he had not sunk to Heng Wen's level of excess."

sentences.zh: 命奪職，發軍台效力。

translations.literal: He ordered his dismissal from office and service at a military penal station.
translations.idiomatic: He was stripped of office and sent to serve at a military penal station.

sentences.zh: 手詔謂：「恆文及一裕罪輕重一歸允當，毋謂一裕以漢吏劾滿洲終兩敗也。」

translations.literal: In a personal edict he said: "The lighter and heavier guilt of Heng Wen and Yiyu each fits the case; do not suppose that because Yiyu, a Han official, impeached a Manchu both were ruined in the end."
translations.idiomatic: In a personal edict he wrote: "Each man's punishment fits his crime; do not imagine that because a Han official impeached a Manchu both were destroyed in the end."

sentences.zh: 一裕呈部請輸金贖罪，會蔣洲、楊灝皆以婪索屬吏坐誅，洲獄具，得同官朋比狀。

translations.literal: Yiyu petitioned the ministry to pay gold to redeem his crime; at the same time Jiang Zhou and Yang Hao were both executed for extorting subordinates, and when Zhou's case was complete it revealed collusion among colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyu petitioned to pay a fine in lieu of punishment; meanwhile Jiang Zhou and Yang Hao were executed for extorting subordinates, and Zhou's completed case exposed a pattern of official collusion.

sentences.zh: 上因謂：「恆文事發自一裕，尚彼勝於此。」

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore said: "Heng Wen's affair began with Yiyu; he is still better than these."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then said: "Heng Wen's case began with Yiyu; Yiyu is still the lesser evil here."

sentences.zh: 特許其納贖。

translations.literal: He specially permitted him to pay redemption.
translations.idiomatic: He specially allowed him to pay a redemption fine.

sentences.zh: 居數年，予三品銜，授河南按察使。

translations.literal: After several years he was given third-rank status and appointed provincial surveillance commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he received third rank and was appointed Henan surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以老罷。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 蔣洲，江南常熟人，大學士廷錫子。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhou was a native of Changshu in Jiangnan, son of Grand Secretary Tingxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhou was from Changshu in Jiangnan, son of Grand Secretary Jiang Tingxi.

sentences.zh: 自主事累擢至山西布政使。

translations.literal: From the post of registrar he was repeatedly promoted to provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: From registrar he rose step by step to provincial administration commissioner of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，就遷巡撫，旋移山東，以塔永寧代。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted in place to governor, then soon transferred to Shandong, with Ta Yongning replacing him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made governor on the spot, then moved to Shandong, with Ta Yongning taking his place.

sentences.zh: 塔永寧劾洲貪縱，虧庫帑鉅萬。

translations.literal: Ta Yongning impeached Zhou for greed and license, with treasury deficits of tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ta Yongning impeached Zhou for corruption and license, citing treasury shortfalls in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 將行，令冀寧道楊龍文、太原知府七賚札諸屬吏納賕彌所虧。

translations.literal: Before departing he ordered Jining intendant Yang Longwen and Taiyuan prefect Qi Sai to notify all subordinates to pay bribes to cover his deficits.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left he had Jining intendant Yang Longwen and Taiyuan prefect Qi Sai instruct subordinates to pay bribes to make up his shortfall.

sentences.zh: 統勳自雲南還，上命馳往會塔永寧按治。

translations.literal: Tongxun returned from Yunnan; the Emperor ordered him to hurry there and join Ta Yongning in the investigation.
translations.idiomatic: When Tongxun returned from Yunnan, the Emperor ordered him to rush back and join Ta Yongning in the investigation.

sentences.zh: 解洲任，逮送山西嚴鞫，得實，誅洲，並及龍文、七賚論絞候。

translations.literal: Zhou was removed from office, arrested and sent to Shanxi for strict interrogation; the facts were proved, Zhou was executed, and Longwen and Qi Sai were sentenced to strangulation after the autumn assizes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou was dismissed, sent to Shanxi for rigorous trial, and executed when the case was proved; Longwen and Qi Sai were sentenced to strangulation after review.

sentences.zh: 諸屬吏虧帑，文職知州硃廷揚等、武職守備武璉等，皆論罪如律。

translations.literal: Subordinates who had deficits in the treasury, including civil prefect Zhu Tingyang and military garrison commander Wu Lian, were all sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinates with treasury shortfalls, civil prefect Zhu Tingyang among them and military commander Wu Lian, were all punished under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 陝西巡撫明德，以前官山西嘗取洲及諸屬吏賕，亦論絞候。

translations.literal: Mingde, governor of Shaanxi, who while previously in Shanxi had taken bribes from Zhou and his subordinates, was also sentenced to strangulation after review.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi governor Mingde, who as a former Shanxi official had taken bribes from Zhou and his subordinates, was likewise sentenced to strangulation after review.

sentences.zh: 上命發甘肅交黃廷桂聽差遣。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered him sent to Gansu and placed under Huang Tinggui for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent him to Gansu under Huang Tinggui's command.

sentences.zh: 楊灝，直隸曲陽人。

translations.literal: Yang Hao was a native of Quyang in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Hao was from Quyang in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 乾隆中，官湖南布政使。

translations.literal: During the Qianlong reign he served as provincial administration commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong he served as Hunan provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時以湖南倉穀濟江南當糴補，灝發穀值百取一二，得金三千有奇。

translations.literal: At the time Hunan granary grain was sent to supply Jiangnan's grain purchases; Hao took one or two percent of the grain value and obtained more than three thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan granary grain was then shipped to Jiangnan for purchase contracts; Hao skimmed one or two percent of the grain payments and pocketed more than three thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳宏謀疏劾，讞實，坐斬。

translations.literal: Governor Chen Hongmou memorialized impeaching him; the case was proved and he was sentenced to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Hongmou impeached him; the case was proved and he was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，秋讞，巡撫蔣炳以灝限內完贓，擬入緩決，上怒，命誅灝，奪炳官，逮京師，論罪坐斬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, at the autumn assizes, Governor Jiang Bing proposed deferred execution because Hao had made restitution within the deadline; the Emperor was angry, ordered Hao executed, stripped Bing of office, had him arrested and sent to the capital, and sentenced him to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, at autumn review, Governor Jiang Bing sought a reprieve because Hao had made restitution on time; the Emperor was furious, ordered Hao executed, stripped Bing of rank, had him brought to the capital, and sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 上以炳意在沽譽，尚未嘗受賄，改戍軍台。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered that Bing's intent was to win reputation and that he had not yet taken bribes, and changed the sentence to service at a military penal station.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged that Bing had sought reputation rather than bribes and had not actually taken graft, and commuted his sentence to service at a military penal station.

sentences.zh: 按察使夔舒亦坐是奪職。

translations.literal: Surveillance commissioner Kui Shu also lost office on this account.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance commissioner Kui Shu was likewise dismissed on this account.

sentences.zh: 高恆，字立齋，滿洲鑲黃旗人，大學士高斌子也。

translations.literal: Gao Heng, style name Lizhai, was a Manchu of the Bordered Yellow Banner, son of Grand Secretary Gao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Heng, styled Lizhai, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow, son of Grand Secretary Gao Bin.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，以廕生授戶部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: Early in the Qianlong reign, as a yinsheng he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted again to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qianlong, as a hereditary candidate he entered the Ministry of Revenue as director and was soon promoted to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 出監山海關、淮安、張家口榷稅，署長蘆鹽政、天津總兵。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise transit duties at Shanhaiguan, Huai'an, and Zhangjiakou, and acted as Changlu salt commissioner and commander at Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised transit levies at Shanhaiguan, Huai'an, and Zhangjiakou, and served as acting Changlu salt commissioner and Tianjin commander.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授兩淮鹽政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed salt commissioner of the Two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was appointed Two Huai salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江蘇巡撫陳宏謀疏言：「海州產鹽盛，請令河東買運配引赴陝西引地行銷。

translations.literal: Jiangsu governor Chen Hongmou memorialized: "Haizhou produces salt in abundance; I ask that Hedong merchants buy and transport it with quota certificates to sell in Shaanxi's licensed territory.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangsu governor Chen Hongmou wrote: "Haizhou's salt output is abundant; let Hedong merchants buy and haul it under quota to sell in Shaanxi's licensed districts.

sentences.zh: 淮北鹽賤，並令淮南商買運適中之地，作常平倉鹽備缺額補配。」

translations.literal: Huainan salt is cheap; also let Huainan merchants buy and transport it to suitable places as ever-normal granary salt to cover shortfalls in quota fulfillment."
translations.idiomatic: North-of-Huai salt is cheaper; also let south-of-Huai merchants buy surplus salt for ever-normal stockpiles to fill quota shortfalls."

sentences.zh: 命高恆會兩江總督尹繼善覆議，尋疏陳：「海洲產鹽盛衰，視天時晴雨，難定成數。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Gao Heng to confer with Liangjiang governor-general Yin Jishan for reconsideration; he soon memorialized: "Haizhou's salt output rises and falls with weather and rain, making fixed quantities hard to set.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Gao Heng to review the plan with Liangjiang governor-general Yin Jishan; Gao soon replied: "Haizhou output depends on weather and cannot be fixed in advance.

sentences.zh: 距陝西三千餘裡，黃河逆流而上，斷難輓運。

translations.literal: It is more than three thousand li from Shaanxi, and hauling upstream on the Yellow River is utterly impracticable.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi lies more than three thousand li away, and hauling salt upstream on the Yellow River is out of the question.

sentences.zh: 自海州出場，經淮、徐、海各屬，皆淮北食鹽口岸；

translations.literal: From Haizhou's salt fields the route passes through Huai, Xu, and Hai jurisdictions, all ports for north-of-Huai table salt;
translations.idiomatic: Salt leaving Haizhou passes through Huai, Xu, and Hai districts, all north-of-Huai consumption ports;

sentences.zh: 徐州以上，又係長蘆引地。

translations.literal: above Xuzhou it is again Changlu licensed territory.
translations.idiomatic: and above Xuzhou the route lies in Changlu licensed territory.

sentences.zh: 恐沿途挾私，淮南額引多，鹽場廣，有盈無絀。

translations.literal: I fear smuggling along the way; south-of-Huai has large quotas and broad salt fields, with surplus rather than shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Smuggling along the route is a risk; south-of-Huai has ample quotas and salt fields and runs a surplus, not a deficit.

sentences.zh: 即淮北鹽價稍賤，加以腳費折耗亦相等。

translations.literal: Even if north-of-Huai salt is somewhat cheaper, with transport costs and wastage the totals are equal.
translations.idiomatic: Even when north-of-Huai salt is cheaper, freight and spoilage bring the cost back to parity.

sentences.zh: 若令淮南銷淮北餘鹽，尤非商情所便。

translations.literal: To have south-of-Huai sell north-of-Huai surplus salt is especially inconvenient to merchants.
translations.idiomatic: Forcing south-of-Huai merchants to sell north-of-Huai surplus salt suits merchant practice least of all.

sentences.zh: 縱發官帑與之收買，亦難強其領運。」

translations.literal: Even if public funds were issued for purchase, it would still be hard to compel them to take transport contracts."
translations.idiomatic: Even with treasury funds to buy the salt, merchants could not be forced to haul it."

sentences.zh: 疏入，上從之。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 湖廣總督李侍堯疏言湖北鹽驟貴，請飭淮商減價。

translations.literal: Huguang governor-general Li Shiyao memorialized that Hubei salt had risen sharply in price and asked that Huai merchants be ordered to reduce prices.
translations.idiomatic: Huguang governor-general Li Shiyao reported that Hubei salt prices had spiked and asked that Two Huai merchants cut their prices.

sentences.zh: 命高恆赴湖北會議。

translations.literal: Gao Heng was ordered to go to Hubei for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Heng was sent to Hubei to confer on the matter.

sentences.zh: 定湖北鹽價，視淮商成本每包以二錢三分一釐為製。

translations.literal: Hubei salt prices were fixed at two mace, three fen, and one li per bundle above Huai merchants' cost.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei salt prices were set at two mace, three fen, and one li per bundle above Two Huai merchants' cost.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授上駟院卿，仍領兩淮鹽政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed director of the Imperial Stud, while still holding the Two Huai salt commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he became director of the Imperial Stud while retaining the Two Huai salt post.

sentences.zh: 三十年，以從兄高晉為兩江總督，當迴避，召署戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, because his cousin Gao Jin was Liangjiang governor-general, he had to withdraw from conflict of interest and was summoned to act as vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year his cousin Gao Jin became Liangjiang governor-general, requiring withdrawal on kinship grounds; he was recalled to serve as acting vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 疏陳整頓綱課，定分季運清獎勵之制，命以告後政普福。

translations.literal: He memorialized on reorganizing salt transport quotas, establishing quarterly clearance and reward rules, and was ordered to inform his successor Pufu.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed reforms to salt transport quotas and quarterly clearance rewards, with orders to pass them to his successor Pufu.

sentences.zh: 尋授總管內務府大臣。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made superintendent of the Imperial Household Department.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，署吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he acted as vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he served as acting vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 是時上屢南巡，兩淮鹽商迎蹕，治行宮揚州，上臨幸，輒留數日乃去，費不貲，頻歲上貢稍華侈。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor made repeated southern tours; Two Huai salt merchants received his progress, built a palace at Yangzhou, and whenever he visited he stayed several days before leaving, at immeasurable cost, with tribute gifts growing somewhat lavish year by year.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was touring the south repeatedly; Two Huai salt merchants built a Yangzhou palace for his visits, where he would stay several days at vast expense, and yearly tribute grew increasingly lavish.

sentences.zh: 高恆為鹽政，陳請預提綱引歲二十萬至四十萬，得旨允行。

translations.literal: As salt commissioner Gao Heng memorialized to advance two hundred thousand to four hundred thousand quota certificates yearly, which was approved by decree.
translations.idiomatic: As salt commissioner, Gao Heng won approval to advance between two hundred thousand and four hundred thousand transport quotas each year.

sentences.zh: 復令諸商每引輸銀三兩為公使錢，因以自私，事皆未報部。

translations.literal: He also ordered all merchants to pay three taels per quota as public-service money and kept it for himself; none of this was reported to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He also made merchants pay three taels per quota as "public-service" fees and pocketed them, reporting none of it to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，兩淮鹽政尤拔世發其弊，上奪高恆官，命江蘇巡撫彰寶會尤拔世按治。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year Two Huai salt commissioner You Bash exposed his abuses; the Emperor stripped Gao Heng of office and ordered Jiangsu governor Zhang Bao to join You Bash in investigation.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year successor commissioner You Bash exposed the abuses; the Emperor dismissed Gao Heng and ordered Jiangsu governor Zhang Bao to investigate with You Bash.

sentences.zh: 諸鹽商具言頻歲上貢及備南巡差共用銀四百六十七萬餘，諸鹽政雖在官久，尚無寄商生息事。

translations.literal: The salt merchants stated in full that over successive years tribute and preparations for southern tour duties together used more than 4.67 million taels; although salt commissioners had long been in office, there was still no practice of depositing funds with merchants for interest.
translations.idiomatic: Salt merchants reported that tribute and southern-tour expenses over the years totaled more than 4.67 million taels; despite long tenures, commissioners had not parked public funds with merchants for interest.

sentences.zh: 上責其未詳盡，下刑部鞫實，高恆嘗受鹽商金，坐誅。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked them for incompleteness, sent the case to the Ministry of Justice for verification, and Gao Heng was found to have taken gold from salt merchants and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor faulted the report as incomplete; the Ministry of Justice confirmed that Gao Heng had taken merchants' gold, and he was executed.

sentences.zh: 普福及鹽運使盧見曾等罪有差。

translations.literal: Pufu and salt transport intendant Lu Jianzeng and others received punishments of varying severity.
translations.idiomatic: Pufu, transport intendant Lu Jianzeng, and others were punished to differing degrees.

sentences.zh: 子高樸，初授武備院員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Gao Pu was first appointed an assistant director in the Armory Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gao Pu began as an assistant director in the Armory Bureau.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中，巡山東漕政。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary and inspected Shandong grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to supervising secretary and inspected Shandong grain transport.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，超擢都察院左副都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he was exceptionally promoted to left vice censor-in-chief of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was leap-promoted to left vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 值月食，救護未至，上諭謂：「高樸年少奮勉，是以加恩擢用，非他人比。

translations.literal: When a lunar eclipse occurred and protective rites were not performed in time, the Emperor instructed: "Gao Pu is young and diligent; that is why I favored him with promotion, unlike others.
translations.idiomatic: During a lunar eclipse the protective rites were late; the Emperor said: "Gao Pu is young and eager—that is why I favored him with promotion, unlike others.

sentences.zh: 乃在朕前有意見長，退後輒圖安逸，豈足副朕造就裁成之意？」

translations.literal: Yet before Me he shows himself grown, and afterward he only seeks ease—how can this fulfill My intent to shape and complete him?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet he plays the grown man before Me and seeks comfort afterward—how does that meet My intent to train and temper him?"

sentences.zh: 吏議奪職，命寬之。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel proposed dismissal, but he was ordered leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Personnel officials proposed dismissal, but the Emperor ordered leniency.

sentences.zh: 遷兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 上錄諸直省道府姓名，密記治行優絀，謂之道府記載，太監高雲從偶洩於外廷。

translations.literal: The Emperor recorded the names of circuit and prefectural officials in all provinces and secretly noted their administrative merit, calling it the Circuit-Prefect Record; eunuch Gao Yuncong accidentally leaked it to the outer court.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor kept a secret register of circuit and prefect officials' performance—the Circuit-Prefect Record—which eunuch Gao Yuncong accidentally leaked to the outer court.

sentences.zh: 左都御史觀保，侍郎蔣賜棨、吳壇、倪承寬嘗因侍班私論其事，高樸聞，具疏劾，上怒，下刑部鞫治。

translations.literal: Left censor-in-chief Guan Bao and vice ministers Jiang Ciqi, Wu Tan, and Ni Chengkuan had once discussed the matter privately while on attendance duty; Gao Pu heard of it and memorialized impeachment in full; the Emperor was angry and sent the case to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Left censor-in-chief Guan Bao and vice ministers Jiang Ciqi, Wu Tan, and Ni Chengkuan had gossiped about the leak while on court duty; Gao Pu impeached them; the Emperor was furious and referred the case to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 尋命誅雲從，貸觀保等，不竟其事。

translations.literal: He soon ordered Yuncong executed and pardoned Guan Bao and the others, not pursuing the matter to the end.
translations.idiomatic: He soon ordered Yuncong executed, pardoned Guan Bao and the others, and dropped the rest of the case.

sentences.zh: 詔謂：「雲從以賤役無忌憚，豈可不亟為整飭以肅紀綱？

translations.literal: An edict said: "Yuncong, a low servant, acted without restraint—how could discipline not be urgently tightened to uphold regulations?
translations.idiomatic: An edict read: "Yuncong, a menial servant, acted without restraint—discipline had to be tightened at once.

sentences.zh: 但不屑因此興大獄，故不復窮治。

translations.literal: Yet I disdained to raise a great prosecution over this, and therefore did not pursue it further.
translations.idiomatic: But I would not launch a major prosecution over it, and pursued it no further.

sentences.zh: 諸大臣豈無見聞，獨高樸為之陳奏，內省應自慚。

translations.literal: Could the grand ministers have been without knowledge? Only Gao Pu memorialized on it; inwardly they ought to feel shame.
translations.idiomatic: Surely other ministers knew of the leak—only Gao Pu reported it; they should examine their own consciences.

sentences.zh: 若因此圖傾高樸，則是自取其死。

translations.literal: If anyone plots to overthrow Gao Pu on this account, he seeks his own death.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who tries to ruin Gao Pu over this courts his own destruction.

sentences.zh: 高樸若沾沾自喜，不知謹懍，轉致妄為，則高雲從即其前車，朕亦不能曲貸也。」

translations.literal: If Gao Pu grows smug and self-satisfied, fails to be cautious, and turns to reckless acts, then Gao Yuncong is his warning—and I cannot bend the law for him either."
translations.idiomatic: If Gao Pu grows smug, neglects caution, and acts recklessly, Yuncong's fate will be his—and I will not spare him."

sentences.zh: 四十一年，命往葉爾羌辦事。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he was ordered to Yarkand on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he was sent to Yarkand on official business.

sentences.zh: 距葉爾羌四百餘裡，有密爾岱山，產玉，舊封禁。

translations.literal: More than four hundred li from Yarkand there is Mount Mi'erdai, which produces jade; it was formerly sealed and forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Some four hundred li from Yarkand stood Mount Mi'erdai, famed for its jade and long sealed off from mining.

sentences.zh: 高樸疏請開採，歲一次。

translations.literal: Gao Pu memorialized requesting to open mining, once per year.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pu memorialized asking permission to open the mines for one annual harvest.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，阿奇木伯克色提巴勒底訴高樸役回民三千采玉，婪索金寶，並盜鬻官玉。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year, Akim Beg Sedibaleidi accused Gao Pu of conscripting three thousand Hui people to mine jade, greedily extorting gold and treasures, and also stealing and selling official jade.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-third year, Akim Beg Sedibaleidi charged Gao Pu with impressing three thousand Hui laborers to mine jade, extorting gold and jewels, and embezzling official jade for private sale.

sentences.zh: 烏什辦事大臣永貴以聞，上命奪官嚴鞫，籍其家，得寄還金玉；

translations.literal: Yonggui, the minister in charge at Ushi, reported it; the Emperor ordered Gao stripped of office and severely interrogated, his property confiscated, and mailed-back gold and jade recovered;
translations.idiomatic: Yonggui, the minister stationed at Ushi, reported the case; the Emperor ordered Gao Pu dismissed, rigorously tried, and his household assets seized, turning up gold and jade he had sent home;

sentences.zh: 永貴又言葉爾羌存銀一萬六千餘、金五百餘。

translations.literal: Yonggui further reported that at Yarkand there remained more than sixteen thousand taels of silver and more than five hundred of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Yonggui further reported over sixteen thousand taels of silver and more than five hundred of gold still on hand at Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 高樸坐誅。

translations.literal: Gao Pu was executed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pu was put to death.

sentences.zh: 方上誅高恆，大學士傅恆從容言乞推慧賢皇貴妃恩貸其死，上曰：「如皇后兄弟犯法，當奈何？」

translations.literal: Just as the Emperor was about to execute Gao Heng, Grand Secretary Fu Heng calmly spoke, asking that the favor owed to Imperial Noble Consort Huixian be extended to spare his life; the Emperor said: "If the Empress's brothers broke the law, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor was about to execute Gao Heng, Grand Secretary Fu Heng calmly asked that the debt owed to Imperial Noble Consort Huixian be invoked to spare him. The Emperor replied: "If the Empress's own brothers violated the law, what would I do then?"

sentences.zh: 傅恆戰栗不敢言。

translations.literal: Fu Heng trembled with fear and dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng shook with fear and said no more.

sentences.zh: 至是，諭曰：「高樸貪婪無忌，罔顧法紀，較其父高恆尤甚，不能念為慧賢皇貴妃侄而稍矜宥也。」

translations.literal: At this time an edict stated: "Gao Pu is greedy beyond restraint and heedless of law and discipline, worse even than his father Gao Heng; I cannot, because he is the nephew of Imperial Noble Consort Huixian, show even slight leniency."
translations.idiomatic: Now an edict declared: "Gao Pu's greed knows no bounds and he scorns the law—worse than his father Gao Heng. I cannot spare him even a little for being Imperial Noble Consort Huixian's nephew."

sentences.zh: 王亶望，山西臨汾人，江蘇巡撫師子。

translations.literal: Wang Danwang, a native of Linfen in Shanxi, was the son of the Governor of Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Danwang, from Linfen in Shanxi, was the son of the Jiangsu governor.

sentences.zh: 自舉人捐納知縣，發甘肅，知山丹、皋蘭諸縣。

translations.literal: Starting as a juren who purchased the office of county magistrate, he was sent to Gansu and served as magistrate of Shandan, Gaolan, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: After purchasing a county magistrate's post as a juren, he was posted to Gansu and served as magistrate of Shandan, Gaolan, and other counties.

sentences.zh: 選授雲南武定知府，引見，命仍往甘肅待缺，除寧夏知府。

translations.literal: Selected and appointed prefect of Wuding in Yunnan, upon imperial audience he was ordered to return to Gansu to await a vacancy and was then appointed prefect of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Named prefect of Wuding in Yunnan, he was received in audience and told to return to Gansu to await a vacancy; he was then appointed prefect of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 累遷浙江布政使，暫署巡撫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Financial Commissioner of Zhejiang and temporarily acted as governor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Financial Commissioner of Zhejiang and briefly served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十八年，上幸天津，亶望貢方物，范金為如意，飾以珠，上拒弗納。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong, when the Emperor visited Tianjin, Danwang presented local products—a ruyi scepter cast in gold and adorned with pearls; the Emperor refused to accept it.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38, when the Emperor traveled to Tianjin, Danwang offered local tribute: a gold ruyi scepter set with pearls. The Emperor declined it.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，移甘肅布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he was transferred to Financial Commissioner of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year he was made Financial Commissioner of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 甘肅舊例，令民輸豆麥，予國子監生，得應試入官，謂之「監糧」，上令罷之。

translations.literal: Gansu had an old practice by which the people contributed beans and wheat to obtain status as students of the Imperial Academy, eligible to take examinations and enter office—this was called "jianliang"; the Emperor ordered it abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Under an old Gansu custom, peasants paid beans and wheat to buy Imperial Academy student status and thus qualify for office—the so-called "jianliang" tribute. The Emperor ordered the practice ended.

sentences.zh: 既，復令肅州、安西收捐如舊例。

translations.literal: Afterwards, collection of donations at Suzhou and Anxi was again permitted as under the old practice.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Suzhou and Anxi were again allowed to collect donations under the former rules.

sentences.zh: 亶望至，申總督勒爾謹，以內地倉儲未實為辭，為疏請諸州縣皆得收捐；

translations.literal: When Danwang arrived, he petitioned Governor-general Le'erjin, citing incomplete inland granary reserves as a reason, and submitted a memorial requesting that all prefectures and counties be allowed to accept donations;
translations.idiomatic: When Danwang arrived, he appealed to Governor-general Le'erjin, claiming inland granaries were unfilled, and memorialized that every prefecture and county be permitted to collect donations again;

sentences.zh: 既，又請於勒爾謹，令民改輸銀。

translations.literal: Afterwards he again requested of Le'erjin that the people be made to pay in silver instead.
translations.idiomatic: He then persuaded Le'erjin to let the people pay in silver rather than grain.

sentences.zh: 歲虛報旱災，妄言以粟治賑，而私其銀，自總督以下皆有分，亶望多取焉。

translations.literal: Each year he falsely reported drought disasters, falsely claiming the grain was for famine relief, but privately kept the silver; from the governor-general down everyone received a share, and Danwang took the largest portion.
translations.idiomatic: Each year he filed false drought reports, pretended the grain was for famine relief, and pocketed the silver instead. Everyone from the governor-general down took a cut, with Danwang keeping the lion's share.

sentences.zh: 議初行，方半載，亶望疏報收捐一萬九千名，得豆麥八十二萬。

translations.literal: When the policy had just begun, after only half a year Danwang memorialized reporting nineteen thousand donations received and eight hundred twenty thousand [units] of beans and wheat obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Barely six months after the scheme began, Danwang reported nineteen thousand donors and 820,000 units of beans and wheat collected.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「甘肅民貧地瘠，安得有二萬人捐監？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The people of Gansu are poor and the land is barren—how could there be twenty thousand grain-donation students?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor objected: "Gansu is poor and its soil is thin—how could twenty thousand men afford to buy Academy status?

sentences.zh: 又安得有如許餘糧？

translations.literal: And how could there be so much surplus grain?
translations.idiomatic: Where would so much surplus grain come from?

sentences.zh: 今半年已得八十二萬，年復一年，經久陳紅，又將安用？

translations.literal: In half a year you already have eight hundred twenty thousand; year after year, as the grain ages and spoils over time, what will it be used for?
translations.idiomatic: You already claim 820,000 in half a year. Year on year it will rot in store—what use is that?

sentences.zh: 即云每歲借給民間，何如留於閭閻，聽其自為流轉？」

translations.literal: Even if you say it is lent out to the people each year, how is that better than leaving it in the villages for them to circulate as they please?"
translations.idiomatic: Even if you lend it out annually, would it not be better to leave the grain in the villages and let people trade it among themselves?"

sentences.zh: 因發「四不可解」詰勒爾謹，勒爾謹飾辭具覆。

translations.literal: Thereupon he issued the "Four Inexplicables" to interrogate Le'erjin; Le'erjin disguised his words in a full reply.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Le'erjin the "Four Inexplicables"—four points he could not fathom—and Le'erjin answered with polished excuses.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「爾等既身任其事，勉力妥為之可也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict: "Since you yourselves bear responsibility for this affair, you need only strive to handle it properly."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "You hold the office—see that you manage it conscientiously."

sentences.zh: 四十二年，擢浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was promoted to Governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he was appointed Governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，上南巡，亶望治供張甚侈。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, when the Emperor made a southern tour, Danwang arranged supplies and accommodations with great extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-fifth year, during the southern tour, Danwang staged lavish provisions and lodging.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「省方問俗，非為遊觀計。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Inspecting the provinces and inquiring into local customs is not meant for sightseeing.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "I tour the provinces to learn local conditions—not for pleasure.

sentences.zh: 今乃添建屋宇，點綴鐙彩，華縟繁費，朕實所不取。」

translations.literal: Now you have built new structures, hung lanterns and decorations—extravagant, elaborate, and costly—I truly do not approve."
translations.idiomatic: You have put up new buildings, hung lanterns and finery—lavish and wasteful. I want none of it."

sentences.zh: 戒毋更如是。

translations.literal: He admonished them not to act thus again.
translations.idiomatic: He warned them not to repeat such excess.

sentences.zh: 亶望旋居母喪，疏請治喪百日後，留塘工自效，上許之。

translations.literal: Danwang soon entered mourning for his mother; he memorialized asking, after a hundred days of mourning, to remain at the seawall works to serve at his own expense, and the Emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Danwang soon went into mourning for his mother and asked to stay on the seawall project after the hundred-day rites; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫李質穎入覲，奏陳海塘事，因及亶望意見不相合，遂言亶望不遣妻拏還裡行喪。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Li Zhiying came for audience, reported on seawall matters, and because his views did not accord with Danwang's, he then said that Danwang had not sent his wife and children home to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhejiang Governor Li Zhiying came to court, he reported on the seawalls and, disagreeing with Danwang, accused him of keeping his wife and children from returning home for the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 上降旨責其忘親越禮，奪官，仍留塘工自效。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict rebuking him for forgetting his parent and transgressing ritual propriety, stripped him of office, but still left him serving at the dike works at his own expense.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him for neglecting filial duty and violating ritual, removed his rank, but let him remain on the seawall project.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，命大學士阿桂如浙江勘工。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year Grand Secretary Agui was ordered to Zhejiang to inspect the works.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year the Emperor sent Grand Secretary Agui to Zhejiang to inspect the seawall project.

sentences.zh: 阿桂疏發杭嘉湖道王燧貪縱、故嘉興知府陳虞盛浮冒狀，上諭曰：「朕上年南巡，入浙江境，即見其侈靡，詰亶望，言虞盛所為。

translations.literal: Agui memorialized exposing the greedy indulgence of Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit Intendant Wang Sui and the fraudulent padding of accounts by former Jiaxing Prefect Chen Yusheng; the Emperor issued an edict: "When I toured south last year and entered Zhejiang, I saw its extravagance and questioned Danwang, who said it was Chen Yusheng's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Agui exposed the greed and lax oversight of Hang-Jia-Hu Circuit Intendant Wang Sui and the padded accounts of former Jiaxing Prefect Chen Yusheng. The Emperor said: "On last year's southern tour, the moment I entered Zhejiang I saw the extravagance. I questioned Danwang, and he blamed Chen Yusheng.

sentences.zh: 今燧等借大差為名，貪縱浮冒，必亶望為之庇護。」

translations.literal: Now Sui and the others, using a major assignment as pretext, are greedy, indulgent, and fraudulent—Danwang must be shielding them."
translations.idiomatic: Now Sui and his circle, under cover of a major project, are greedy, reckless, and fraudulent—Danwang must be protecting them."

sentences.zh: 命逮燧嚴鞫。

translations.literal: He ordered Sui arrested and severely interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wang Sui arrested and rigorously tried.

sentences.zh: 會河州回蘇四十三為亂，勒爾謹師屢敗，亦被逮。

translations.literal: Meanwhile the Hezhou Hui rebel Su Forty-three rose in revolt; Le'erjin's troops were repeatedly defeated, and he too was arrested.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Hezhou Hui leader Su Forty-three rebelled; Le'erjin's forces suffered repeated defeats, and he was arrested as well.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿桂出視師，未即至，命尚書和珅先焉，和珅疏言入境即遇雨，阿桂報師行亦屢言雨。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Agui went out to take command of the army but had not yet arrived; the Emperor ordered Minister Heshen to go first. Heshen memorialized that upon entering the province he immediately encountered rain, and Agui's reports on the army's march likewise repeatedly mentioned rain.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Agui set out to command the campaign but had not yet arrived; Minister Heshen was sent ahead. Heshen reported rain the moment he crossed the border, and Agui's dispatches on the march likewise kept citing rain.

sentences.zh: 上因疑甘肅頻歲報旱不實，諭阿桂及總督李侍堯令具實以聞。

translations.literal: The Emperor therefore suspected that Gansu's drought reports in successive years were false, and issued an edict Agui and Governor Li Shiyao to report the facts in full.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then suspected years of false drought reports from Gansu and ordered Agui and Governor Li Shiyao to send the truth.

sentences.zh: 阿桂、侍堯疏發亶望等令監糧改輸銀及虛銷賑粟自私諸狀，上怒甚，遣侍郎楊魁如浙江會巡撫陳輝祖召亶望嚴鞫，籍其家，得金銀逾百萬。

translations.literal: Agui and Shiyao memorialized exposing Danwang and others for ordering the change from jianliang to silver payment and falsely writing off relief grain for private gain, and the like; the Emperor was furious and dispatched Vice Minister Yang Kui to Zhejiang to join Governor Chen Huizu in summoning Danwang for severe interrogation and confiscating his property, yielding gold and silver exceeding one million.
translations.idiomatic: Agui and Shiyao exposed how Danwang and his circle had converted jianliang to silver payments and falsified famine relief to enrich themselves. Enraged, the Emperor sent Vice Minister Yang Kui to Zhejiang with Governor Chen Huizu to try Danwang and seize his estate, which held over a million taels in gold and silver.

sentences.zh: 上幸熱河，逮亶望、勒爾謹及甘肅布政使王廷贊赴行在，令諸大臣會鞫。

translations.literal: While the Emperor was at Rehe, Danwang, Le'erjin, and Gansu Financial Commissioner Wang Tingzan were arrested and brought to the temporary palace, and the grand ministers were ordered to conduct a joint trial.
translations.idiomatic: At Rehe the Emperor had Danwang, Le'erjin, and Gansu Financial Commissioner Wang Tingzan brought to the traveling court and ordered the grand ministers to try them jointly.

sentences.zh: 亶望具服發議監糧改輸銀，令蘭州知府蔣全迪示意諸州縣偽報旱災，迫所轄道府具結申轉；

translations.literal: Danwang fully confessed to initiating the change from jianliang to silver payment, having Lanzhou Prefect Jiang Quandi instruct the prefectures and counties to falsely report drought disasters, and forcing the circuit and prefects under his jurisdiction to sign certifications and submit them upward;
translations.idiomatic: Danwang confessed to proposing the switch from jianliang to silver, directing Lanzhou Prefect Jiang Quandi to have prefectures and counties file false drought reports, and coercing his circuit and prefectural subordinates to certify and forward the fraud;

sentences.zh: 在官尚奢侈，皋蘭知縣程棟為支應，諸州縣饣鬼賂率以千萬計。

translations.literal: While in office he was still extravagant; Gaolan Magistrate Cheng Dong handled disbursements, and bribes from the various prefectures and counties typically amounted to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Even in office he lived lavishly; Gaolan Magistrate Cheng Dong managed his expenses, and bribes from prefectures and counties routinely ran to tens of thousands of taels.

sentences.zh: 獄定，上命斬亶望，賜勒爾謹自裁，廷贊論絞，並命即蘭州斬全迪；

translations.literal: When the case was decided, the Emperor ordered Danwang beheaded, granted Le'erjin permission to commit suicide, sentenced Tingzan to strangulation, and also ordered Quandi beheaded at once in Lanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: When judgment was rendered, the Emperor ordered Danwang executed, allowed Le'erjin to take his own life, sentenced Wang Tingzan to strangulation, and had Jiang Quandi beheaded on the spot in Lanzhou;

sentences.zh: 遂令阿桂按治諸州縣，冒賑至二萬以上皆死，於是坐斬者棟等二十二人，餘譴黜有差。

translations.literal: Agui was then ordered to investigate all prefectures and counties; those who falsely claimed relief exceeding twenty thousand were all executed—twenty-two including Cheng Dong were beheaded, and the rest were demoted or dismissed to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Agui was then sent to investigate every prefecture and county; anyone who embezzled more than twenty thousand in relief funds was put to death. Twenty-two men, including Cheng Dong, were beheaded; the rest were punished or dismissed according to their guilt.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「此二十二人之死，皆亶望導之使陷於法，與亶望殺之何異？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The deaths of these twenty-two men were all led by Danwang into violation of the law—how is that different from Danwang killing them?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "These twenty-two died because Danwang led them into crime—what difference is there between that and murder by his hand?"

sentences.zh: 令奪亶望子裘等官，發伊犁，幼子逮下刑部獄，年至十二，即次第遣發，逃者斬。

translations.literal: He ordered Danwang's sons Qiu and others stripped of office and sent to Ili; the youngest son was imprisoned in the Ministry of Justice—when he reached twelve he would be sent away in succession, and anyone who fled would be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He stripped Danwang's sons, including Qiu, of their posts and exiled them to Ili; the youngest was held in the Ministry of Justice prison and, on turning twelve, would be sent away in turn—flight meant death.

sentences.zh: 陝甘總督李侍堯續發得賕諸吏，又誅閔鵷元等十一人，罪董熙等六人。

translations.literal: Shaanxi-Gansu Governor Li Shiyao further exposed officials who had taken bribes; Min Yuan and eleven others were also executed, and Dong Xi and six others were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi-Gansu Governor Li Shiyao exposed still more bribe-taking officials; Min Yuan and eleven others were executed, and Dong Xi and six more were sentenced.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，上將歸政，國史館進師傳。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, as the Emperor was about to abdicate, the Historiographical Institute submitted the masters' biographies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year, as the Emperor prepared to abdicate, the Historiographical Institute presented the collected biographies of his teachers.

sentences.zh: 上覽其治績，乃赦亶望子還，幼者罷勿遣，謂「勿令師絕嗣也」。

translations.literal: The Emperor reviewed Danwang's record of governance and thereupon pardoned Danwang's sons to return; the youngest was exempted from exile, saying "Let not the Shike line be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Reading Danwang's record of service, the Emperor pardoned his sons and let them return; the youngest was spared further exile, saying, "Do not let his father's line die out."

sentences.zh: 勒爾謹，宜特墨氏，滿洲鑲白旗人。

translations.literal: Le'erjin, of the Yitemo clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Le'erjin, of the Yitemo clan, belonged to the Plain White Banner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆初，以繙譯進士授刑部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: In early Qianlong, as a translation jinshi he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was promoted to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: In early Qianlong he passed the translation jinshi examination, entered the Ministry of Justice as a principal clerk, and rose to vice director.

sentences.zh: 外授直隸天津道。

translations.literal: He was sent out as intendant of Tianjin Circuit in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted outside the capital as intendant of Tianjin Circuit in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 累遷陝甘總督。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，河州回黃國其、王伏林為亂，馳往捕治，誅國其、伏林及其徒四百餘人。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year the Hezhou Hui Huang Guoqi and Wang Fulin rebelled; he galloped to capture and suppress them, executing Guoqi, Fulin, and more than four hundred of their followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year the Hezhou Hui leaders Huang Guoqi and Wang Fulin rebelled; he rushed to suppress them and executed Guoqi, Fulin, and over four hundred followers.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，循化回蘇四十三復起，勒爾謹令蘭州知府楊士璣、河州協副將新柱率二百人往捕，為所戕，遂破河州。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year the Xunhua Hui Su Forty-three rose again; Le'erjin ordered Lanzhou Prefect Yang Shiji and Hezhou Assistant Brigade Commander Xin Zhu to lead two hundred men to capture him; they were killed, and the rebels then overran Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year Su Forty-three of Xunhua rebelled again. Le'erjin sent Lanzhou Prefect Yang Shiji and Hezhou Assistant Brigade Commander Xin Zhu with two hundred men to arrest him; they were slaughtered, and the rebels took Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 勒爾謹赴援，聞賊將自小道徑攻蘭州，引還城守。

translations.literal: Le'erjin went to reinforce, but hearing the bandits would attack Lanzhou by a side path, he withdrew to hold the city.
translations.idiomatic: Le'erjin marched to relieve the siege, but hearing the rebels would strike Lanzhou by a back route, he pulled back to defend the city.

sentences.zh: 上責勒爾謹觀望失機，奪官；

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked Le'erjin for standing by and losing the opportunity, and stripped him of office;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor blamed Le'erjin for hesitation and missed chances, and removed him from office;

sentences.zh: 下刑部論斬，上命改監候，卒坐亶望獄死。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Justice recommended decapitation; the Emperor ordered it changed to imprisonment awaiting execution; he ultimately died in prison in the Danwang case.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Justice recommended execution; the Emperor commuted the sentence to imprisonment awaiting execution. He ultimately died in prison during the Danwang affair.

sentences.zh: 陳輝祖又以籍亶望家匿金玉器，譴誅。

translations.literal: Chen Huizu was also condemned and executed for concealing gold and jade vessels when confiscating Danwang's property.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Huizu was condemned and executed for hiding gold and jade when Danwang's estate was inventoried.

sentences.zh: 輝祖，湖南祁陽人，兩廣總督大受子也。

translations.literal: Huizu, a native of Qiyang in Hunan, was the son of Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi Da Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Huizu, from Qiyang in Hunan, was the son of Da Shou, Governor-General of Guangdong and Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 以廕生授戶部員外郎，遷郎中。

translations.literal: As a yin student he was appointed vice director in the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: Through hereditary privilege he entered the Ministry of Revenue as a vice director and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 外授河南陳州知府。

translations.literal: Sent out, he served as prefect of Chenzhou in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Henan as prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷閩浙總督，兼領浙江巡撫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang, concurrently holding the post of Governor of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang, also serving as Governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 亶望獄起，輝祖弟嚴祖為甘肅知縣，獄辭連染。

translations.literal: When the Danwang case arose, Huizu's younger brother Yan Zu was a county magistrate in Gansu, and the case testimony implicated him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Danwang case broke, Huizu's brother Yan Zu, a Gansu county magistrate, was implicated in the testimony.

sentences.zh: 上以輝祖當知狀，詰之，不敢言，詔嚴切，乃具陳平日實有所聞，懼嚴祖且得罪，隱忍未聞上，因請罪，降三品頂戴留任。

translations.literal: The Emperor believed Huizu must have known of the affair and interrogated him; he did not dare speak. After stern edicts, he finally stated in full that he had indeed heard something of it in daily life but, fearing Yan Zu would also be punished, had endured in silence and not reported to the Emperor; he therefore pleaded guilty and was demoted by three ranks of hat finial while retained in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor believed Huizu must have known and pressed him; at first he would not speak. Under stern edicts he finally admitted he had heard rumors but, fearing for Yan Zu, had kept silent. He pleaded guilty and was demoted three hat-ranks but kept his post.

sentences.zh: 時安徽巡撫閔鶚元亦坐其弟鵷元，與輝祖同譴。

translations.literal: At the time Anhui Governor Min E yuan was also punished because of his younger brother Min Yuan, receiving the same reprimand as Huizu.
translations.idiomatic: Anhui Governor Min Eyuan was punished at the same time because of his brother Min Yuan and received the same rebuke as Huizu.

sentences.zh: 既，布政使盛柱疏言檢校亶望家入官物與原冊有異同，命大學士阿桂按治，具得輝祖隱匿私易狀，論斬。

translations.literal: Afterwards, Financial Commissioner Sheng Zhu memorialized that items from Danwang's confiscated property entering official inventory differed from the original register; the Emperor ordered Grand Secretary Agui to investigate, fully established Huizu's concealment and private exchange, and sentenced him to decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Later Financial Commissioner Sheng Zhu reported discrepancies between Danwang's seized property and the official inventory. Agui was ordered to investigate, proved Huizu had concealed and swapped items, and recommended execution.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「輝祖罪固無可逭，然與亶望較，終不同。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Huizu's guilt certainly cannot be escaped, but compared with Danwang, he is ultimately not the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Huizu's guilt is undeniable, yet compared with Danwang he is not the same man.

sentences.zh: 傳云：'與其有聚斂之臣，寧有盜臣。

translations.literal: The Classic says: 'Better to have a thieving minister than a minister who amasses wealth.'
translations.idiomatic: The Classic says: 'Better a thieving minister than one who squeezes the people dry.'

sentences.zh: '輝祖盜臣耳。

translations.literal: Huizu is merely a thieving minister.
translations.idiomatic: Huizu is only a thief.

sentences.zh: 亦命改監候。」

translations.literal: He was also ordered to imprisonment awaiting execution."
translations.idiomatic: The sentence was likewise commuted to imprisonment awaiting execution."

sentences.zh: 四十七年，浙江巡撫福崧奏桐鄉民因徵漕聚眾閧縣庭，輝祖寬其罪，次年乃復閧。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year Zhejiang Governor Fu Song memorialized that the people of Tongxiang, on account of grain tribute collection, had gathered in a mob at the county yamen; Huizu treated their offenses leniently, and the next year they gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year Zhejiang Governor Fu Song reported that Tongxiang peasants had mobbed the county yamen over grain tribute; Huizu treated them leniently, and the next year they rioted again.

sentences.zh: 閩浙總督富勒渾奏兩省諸州縣虧倉穀，福建水師提督黃仕簡奏台灣民互鬥，於是上罪輝祖牟利營私，兩省庶政皆廢弛貽誤，罪無異亶望，賜自裁。

translations.literal: Governor-General Fu Lehun of Fujian and Zhejiang memorialized that various prefectures and counties in both provinces were deficient in granary grain; Fujian Naval Commander Huang Shijian memorialized that the people of Taiwan were fighting one another—in consequence the Emperor convicted Huizu of profiting for himself and neglecting duty, held that civil administration in both provinces had been lax and mishandled with lasting harm, judged his guilt no different from Danwang's, and granted him permission to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Fu Lehun reported granary shortfalls across both provinces; Fujian Naval Commander Huang Shijian reported factional fighting in Taiwan. The Emperor then found Huizu guilty of profiteering and neglect, held that civil government in both provinces had collapsed under him, judged his crime equal to Danwang's, and granted him suicide.

sentences.zh: 五十三年，又以湖北吏治闒茸，弊始輝祖為巡撫時，戍其子伊犁。

translations.literal: In the fifty-third year, because official governance in Hubei was neglected and lax—malpractices that began when Huizu was governor—his son was exiled to Ili.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-third year, citing the slipshod administration of Hubei—abuses that began when Huizu was governor there—his son was exiled to Ili.

sentences.zh: 乾隆季年，諸貪吏首亶望，次則鄭源鸘。

translations.literal: In the late Qianlong era, among the greedy officials Danwang ranked first and Zheng Yuanhuang second.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong's final years, Wang Danwang stood first among corrupt officials; Zheng Yuanhuang was second.

sentences.zh: 源鸘，直隸豐潤人。

translations.literal: Yuanhuang, a native of Fengrun in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhuang was from Fengrun in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 以貢生授戶部主事，累遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: As a tribute student he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and was repeatedly promoted to Financial Commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Entering as a tribute student in the Ministry of Revenue, he rose to Financial Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 仁宗既誅和珅，有言源鸘貪黷狀，下巡撫姜晟按治。

translations.literal: After the Jiaqing Emperor had executed Heshen, reports were made of Yuanhuang's corrupt conduct, and the case was referred to Governor Jiang Sheng for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jiaqing Emperor executed Heshen, reports of Yuanhuang's corruption reached the throne, and Governor Jiang Sheng was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 源鸘具服收發庫項，加扣平餘，數逾八萬；

translations.literal: Yuanhuang fully confessed to receiving and disbursing treasury funds while adding deducted surpluses, the amount exceeding eighty thousand;
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhuang confessed to skimming surplus balances when handling treasury receipts and payments, totaling more than eighty thousand taels;

sentences.zh: 署內眷屬幾三百人，自蓄優伶，服官奢侈。

translations.literal: The dependents in his yamen numbered nearly three hundred; he kept his own opera troupe and lived extravagantly in office.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly three hundred dependents crowded his yamen; he maintained a private opera troupe and lived in lavish style.

sentences.zh: 上宣示源鸘罪狀，因言：「諸直省大吏宴會酒食，率以囑首縣，首縣复斂於諸州縣。

translations.literal: The Emperor published Yuanhuang's crimes and said: "When great officials of the various provinces hold banquets and feasts, they invariably instruct the chief county magistrate, who in turn levies the various prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor announced Yuanhuang's crimes and said: "When provincial governors feast, they routinely charge the seat county magistrate, who then levies every prefecture and county under him.

sentences.zh: 率皆朘小民之脂膏，供大吏之娛樂，展轉苛派，受害仍在吾民。

translations.literal: Nearly all squeeze the fat and marrow from the common people to supply the great officials' entertainments; through repeated exactions the victims are still our people.
translations.idiomatic: In the end it is the common people's sweat and blood that pay for the grandees' pleasures—layer upon layer of exactions, and the suffering falls on our people still.

sentences.zh: 通諭諸直省，令悛改積習。」

translations.literal: Issue a general edict to all provinces ordering reform of these entrenched habits."
translations.idiomatic: Let a general edict go out to every province commanding them to abandon these entrenched abuses."

sentences.zh: 尋命斬源鸘。

translations.literal: He soon ordered Yuanhuang beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhuang was soon executed.

sentences.zh: 國泰，富察氏，滿洲鑲白旗人，四川總督文綬子也。

translations.literal: Guotai, of the Fuca clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain White Banner and the son of Sichuan Governor Wen Shou.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai, of the Fuca clan and the Plain White Banner, was the son of Sichuan Governor Wen Shou.

sentences.zh: 國泰初授刑部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: Guotai was first appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice, then twice promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai entered the Ministry of Justice as a principal clerk and was twice promoted to director.

sentences.zh: 外擢山東按察使，遷布政使。

translations.literal: Sent out, he was elevated to surveillance commissioner of Shandong, then promoted to financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Shandong, he became surveillance commissioner and then financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十八年，文綬官陝甘總督，奉命按前四川總督阿爾泰縱子明德布婪索屬吏，徇不以實陳，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year of Qianlong, Wen Shou held office as Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu; ordered to investigate former Sichuan Governor A'ertai for indulging his son Mingde in greedy extortion of subordinate officials and presenting a false report, he was exiled to Ili.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 38, Wen Shou served as Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu. Ordered to investigate former Sichuan Governor A'ertai for shielding his son Mingde's extortion of subordinates and filing a false report, he was exiled to Ili.

sentences.zh: 國泰具疏謝，請從父戍所贖父罪。

translations.literal: Guotai submitted a memorial in apology and asked to follow his father to the place of exile to redeem his father's guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai memorialized in apology and asked to join his father in exile to atone for his crime.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「汝無罪，何必惶懼？」

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict: "You are without guilt—why need you fear?"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "You are guilty of nothing—why such fear?"

sentences.zh: 四十二年，遷巡撫。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-second year he was made governor.

sentences.zh: 國泰紈褲子，早貴，遇屬吏不以禮，小不當意，輒呵斥。

translations.literal: Guotai was a spoiled scion who rose early to high rank; he did not treat subordinate officials with courtesy, and at the slightest displeasure would berate them.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai was a pampered young noble who rose early to power; he showed subordinates no courtesy and berated them over the smallest slight.

sentences.zh: 布政使於易簡事之諂，至長跪白事。

translations.literal: Financial Commissioner Yu Yijian flattered him in his service; when reporting business he would even kneel at length.
translations.idiomatic: Financial Commissioner Yu Yijian fawned on him so abjectly that he would kneel when presenting business.

sentences.zh: 易簡，江蘇金壇人，大學士敏中弟也。

translations.literal: Yijian, a native of Jintan in Jiangsu, was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian, from Jintan in Jiangsu, was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Minzhong.

sentences.zh: 大學士阿桂等以國泰乖張，請改京朝官。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries including Agui, citing Guotai's perversity, requested that he be transferred to a capital office.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries including Agui, finding Guotai insubordinate and overbearing, asked that he be moved to a post in the capital.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，上為召易簡詣京師問狀，易簡為國泰力辨。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year the Emperor had Yijian summoned to the capital to question him; Yijian vigorously argued in Guotai's defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year the Emperor summoned Yijian to the capital to answer for his conduct, and Yijian spoke out forcefully on Guotai's behalf.

sentences.zh: 上降旨戒國泰馭屬吏當寬嚴得中，令警惕改悔。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict warning Guotai that in governing subordinate officials he must balance leniency and severity, and ordered him to be vigilant and repent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent down an edict admonishing Guotai to govern his subordinates with a proper balance of leniency and strictness, and commanded him to take heed and reform.

sentences.zh: 會文綬复官四川總督，以啯匪為亂，再戍伊犁，國泰未具疏謝。

translations.literal: When Wen Shou was restored as Governor of Sichuan but then exiled again to Ili on account of Gao bandit disorder, Guotai failed to submit a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Shou was reappointed Governor of Sichuan but then sent back into exile at Ili after trouble with Gao bandits, Guotai never submitted the required memorial of acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 居月餘，疏謝賜鹿肉，上詰責。

translations.literal: After more than a month he submitted a memorial thanking the Emperor for venison, and the Emperor rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later he memorialized to thank the Emperor for a gift of venison, and the Emperor sharply censured him.

sentences.zh: 國泰請納養廉為父贖，並乞治罪，上寬之。

translations.literal: Guotai asked to surrender his integrity stipend to redeem his father and also begged to be punished; the Emperor showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai offered to forfeit his integrity salary to atone for his father and asked to be punished as well; the Emperor was merciful.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，御史錢灃劾國泰及易簡貪縱營私，徵賂諸州縣，諸州縣倉庫皆虧缺。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year Censor Qian Feng impeached Guotai and Yijian for greedy indulgence and private profiteering, extorting bribes from prefectures and counties; the granaries of all prefectures and counties showed deficits.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-seventh year Censor Qian Feng impeached Guotai and Yijian for greed, lax discipline, and private profiteering, charging that they had extorted bribes from prefectures and counties until every granary in the province was in deficit.

sentences.zh: 上命尚書和珅、左都御史劉墉按治，並令灃與俱。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Minister Heshen and Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong to investigate, and directed Feng to accompany them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Minister Heshen and Censor-in-Chief Liu Yong to conduct the investigation and commanded Feng to go with them.

sentences.zh: 和珅故袒國泰；

translations.literal: Heshen deliberately shielded Guotai;
translations.idiomatic: Heshen deliberately took Guotai's side;

sentences.zh: 墉持正，以國泰虐其鄉，右灃。

translations.literal: Liu Yong held to righteousness; because Guotai had tyrannized his home district, he sided with Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong stood firm on principle; remembering how Guotai had abused his own home district, he supported Feng.

sentences.zh: 驗歷城庫銀銀色不一，得借市充庫狀。

translations.literal: On examining the treasury silver of Licheng and finding its fineness inconsistent, they obtained evidence of market silver borrowed to fill the vault.
translations.idiomatic: When they inspected Licheng's treasury silver and found the fineness inconsistent, they uncovered proof that market silver had been borrowed to pad the vault.

sentences.zh: 語互詳灃傳。

translations.literal: The full account is given in Feng's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The details are set out at length in Feng's biography.

sentences.zh: 國泰具服婪索諸屬吏，數輒至千萬。

translations.literal: Guotai fully confessed to greedy extortion from subordinate officials, sums often reaching ten million.
translations.idiomatic: Guotai fully confessed to extorting his subordinates, with individual amounts often running into the millions.

sentences.zh: 易簡諂國泰，上詰不敢以實對。

translations.literal: Yijian had flattered Guotai; when the Emperor questioned him, he did not dare answer truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: Yijian had fawned on Guotai, and when the Emperor pressed him he did not dare tell the truth.

sentences.zh: 獄定，皆論斬，上命改監候，逮系刑部獄。

translations.literal: When the case was decided, all were sentenced to decapitation; the Emperor ordered commutation to imprisonment awaiting execution, and they were detained in the Ministry of Justice prison.
translations.idiomatic: When judgment was rendered all were sentenced to death, but the Emperor commuted the sentence to imprisonment awaiting execution and had them held in the Ministry of Justice jail.

sentences.zh: 巡撫明興疏言通察諸州縣倉庫，虧二百萬有奇，皆國泰、易簡在官時事。

translations.literal: Governor Mingxing memorialized that a thorough inspection of prefectural and county granaries showed deficits exceeding two million, all dating from Guotai's and Yijian's time in office.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Mingxing reported that a province-wide audit of granaries had uncovered deficits of more than two million taels, all incurred while Guotai and Yijian were in office.

sentences.zh: 上命即獄中詰國泰等，國泰等言因王倫亂，諸州縣以公使錢佐軍興，乃虧及倉庫。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Guotai and the others questioned in prison; they said that because of Wang Lun's rebellion, prefectures and counties had used public funds to support military levies, which caused deficits in the granaries.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Guotai and the others interrogated in prison; they claimed that during Wang Lun's rebellion prefectures and counties had diverted public funds to support the war effort, and that this had drained the granaries.

sentences.zh: 上以「王倫亂起滅不過一月，即謂軍興事急，何多至二百萬？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Wang Lun's rebellion rose and was suppressed in little more than a month— even if military levies were urgent, how could deficits reach two million?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied: "Wang Lun's rebellion broke out and was put down in barely a month. Even if war expenses were pressing, how could losses run to two million?

sentences.zh: 即有之，當具疏以實聞。

translations.literal: Even if such losses existed, you should have submitted a memorial reporting the facts.
translations.idiomatic: If such losses truly existed, you should have memorialized the throne with a full and truthful account.

sentences.zh: 國泰、易簡罔上行私，視諸屬吏虧帑恝置不問，罪與王亶望等均」。

translations.literal: Guotai and Yijian deceived the throne for private gain and looked on unconcerned while subordinate officials depleted the treasury—their crime equals that of Wang Danwang and the others."
translations.idiomatic: Guotai and Yijian deceived the throne to serve themselves and turned a blind eye while their subordinates emptied the public coffers. Their guilt is on a par with Wang Danwang's."

sentences.zh: 命即獄中賜自裁。

translations.literal: He ordered that they be granted suicide immediately in prison.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them granted the privilege of suicide there in prison.

sentences.zh: 郝碩，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Hao Shuo was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Shuo was a Han Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow.

sentences.zh: 父郝玉麟，官兩江總督。

translations.literal: His father Hao Yulin served as Governor-General of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hao Yulin had been Governor-General of Liangjiang.

sentences.zh: 郝碩襲騎都尉世職，授戶部員外郎，直軍機處，遷郎中。

translations.literal: Hao Shuo inherited the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, was appointed an assistant department director in the Board of Revenue, served on the Grand Council staff, and was promoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Shuo inherited the hereditary rank of Commandant of Cavalry, entered the Board of Revenue as an assistant department director, served on the Grand Council staff, and rose to department director.

sentences.zh: 外授山東登萊青道，三遷江西巡撫。

translations.literal: Posted outside the capital as intendant of Deng-Lai-Qing Circuit in Shandong, he was thrice promoted to Governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as intendant of the Deng-Lai-Qing circuit in Shandong, he was promoted three times until he became Governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 將朝京師，以行李不具，徵屬吏納賕。

translations.literal: When about to go to the capital for audience, finding his luggage insufficient, he extorted bribes from subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: As he prepared to go to the capital for audience, his traveling funds fell short, so he squeezed bribes from his subordinates.

sentences.zh: 四十九年，兩江總督薩載論劾，逮京師鞫實。

translations.literal: In the forty-ninth year Governor-General Sa Zai memorialized impeaching him; he was brought to the capital and the charges verified.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-ninth year Governor-General Sa Zai impeached him by memorial; he was brought to the capital and the case proved.

sentences.zh: 上謂：「郝碩罪同國泰，國泰小有才，地方事尚知料理。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Hao Shuo's crime equals Guotai's. Guotai had a little talent and still knew how to manage local affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Hao Shuo's offense is the same as Guotai's. Guotai had some ability and at least knew how to handle provincial business.

sentences.zh: 郝碩嘗朝行在，問以地方事，不知所對。

translations.literal: Hao Shuo once attended audience at the traveling palace; when asked about local affairs, he did not know how to answer.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Shuo once came to audience at the traveling palace, and when questioned about local affairs he had nothing coherent to say.

sentences.zh: 不意复貪婪若是！

translations.literal: I never expected him to be so greedy again!
