translations.idiomatic: Who would have thought he could be so greedy!

sentences.zh: 且郝碩託辭求賂，正國泰事敗時，乃明知故蹈，無復忌憚。

translations.literal: Moreover, Hao Shuo used pretexts to solicit bribes precisely when Guotai's case had just failed—knowing the risk, he still went ahead, no longer having any fear.
translations.idiomatic: And Hao Shuo contrived excuses to extort bribes right when Guotai's downfall was fresh—he knew the danger and did it anyway, utterly without restraint.

sentences.zh: 即視國泰例賜自裁。」

translations.literal: He was immediately sentenced under Guotai's precedent and granted suicide."
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately sentenced by Guotai's precedent and granted suicide."

sentences.zh: 因通諭諸直省督撫，當持名節，畏憲典，以國泰、郝碩為戒。

translations.literal: A general edict was then issued to all provincial governors and governors-general that they must uphold reputation and integrity, fear the law, and take Guotai and Hao Shuo as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: A general edict went out to governors and governor-generals in every province telling them to guard their honor, respect the law, and take Guotai and Hao Shuo as a warning.

sentences.zh: 良卿，富察氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Liang Qing, of the Fuca clan, was a Manchu of the Plain White Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qing, of the Fuca clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain White.

sentences.zh: 乾隆七年進士，授戶部主事，遷郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the seventh year of Qianlong, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of Revenue and promoted to department director.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination in Qianlong 7, he entered the Board of Revenue as a principal clerk and rose to department director.

sentences.zh: 外授直隸通永道，累遷貴州布政使。

translations.literal: Posted outside as intendant of Tong-Yong Circuit in Zhili, he was cumulatively promoted to Financial Commissioner of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posted out as intendant of the Tong-Yong circuit in Zhili, he worked his way up to Financial Commissioner of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，命署巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was ordered to act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was appointed acting governor.

sentences.zh: 師徵緬甸，良卿董台站。

translations.literal: When the army marched against Burma, Liang Qing oversaw the relay stations.
translations.idiomatic: During the Burma campaign Liang Qing supervised the relay stations.

sentences.zh: 上諭良卿：「師行供頓有資民力者，覈實奏聞。」

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Liang Qing: "Where troop movements and supply arrangements draw on the people's labor, verify the facts and report."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told Liang Qing: "Wherever marching troops and their supplies impose on the people, investigate the facts and report them."

sentences.zh: 良卿疏言：「此項多鄉保措辦，銀數多寡參差，無從覈算。」

translations.literal: Liang Qing memorialized: "These matters are mostly handled by village headmen; the silver amounts vary widely and cannot be audited."
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qing replied in a memorial: "Most of this is arranged through village headmen; the sums vary too widely to be audited."

sentences.zh: 上謂：「師行供頓有資民力，亦當官為檢覈。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Where troop movements and supply arrangements draw on the people's labor, officials must still inspect and verify.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Even when marching troops and supplies lean on the people, officials must still inspect and verify.

sentences.zh: 若以鄉保措辦遂置不問，民瘼何所仰賴？

translations.literal: If because village headmen handle arrangements you leave the matter alone, on what can the people's grievances rely?
translations.idiomatic: If you dismiss it because village headmen handle the arrangements, where can the people turn with their grievances?

sentences.zh: 且吏役因以為奸，又何所不至耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, clerks and runners will take the opportunity for corruption—what will they not dare to do?
translations.idiomatic: And clerks and runners will seize the chance for abuse—what limit would there be to their misconduct?

sentences.zh: 良卿以布政使署巡撫，何得諉為不知？」

translations.literal: Liang Qing, acting as governor while holding the rank of financial commissioner—how can he plead ignorance?"
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qing is acting governor while still financial commissioner—how can he claim not to know?"

sentences.zh: 下吏議，當降調，命改奪官，仍留任。

translations.literal: The case was referred to the Board of Punishments, which recommended demotion and transfer; the order was changed to stripping of rank while retaining him in office.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Punishments recommended demotion, but the Emperor instead stripped him of rank while keeping him in post.

sentences.zh: 既，上發帑佐軍需，良卿請確查散給，上詰良卿：「既言無從覈算，何能確查散給？」

translations.literal: Later the Emperor released treasury funds to assist military needs; Liang Qing asked to verify and distribute them strictly. The Emperor questioned Liang Qing: "If you say audit is impossible, how can you verify and distribute strictly?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the Emperor released treasury funds for the army, and Liang Qing asked to audit and distribute them carefully. The Emperor challenged him: "You said these sums could not be audited—how then can you audit and distribute them carefully?"

sentences.zh: 命留供續發官軍。

translations.literal: He ordered the funds held for continued disbursement to the official army.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the funds held back for continued disbursement to the troops.

sentences.zh: 良卿又疏陳貴州兵極能走險耐瘴，請募五千人習槍砲、藤牌備徵發。

translations.literal: Liang Qing also memorialized that Guizhou troops excel at traversing dangerous terrain and enduring malarial climate, and asked to recruit five thousand men to train with muskets, cannon, and rattan shields for deployment.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qing also reported that Guizhou soldiers were exceptionally hardy on difficult terrain and in malarial country, and asked to recruit five thousand men to drill with muskets, cannon, and rattan shields for future campaigns.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其盡心，賜孔雀翎。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his dedication and granted him a peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended his diligence and awarded him a peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 尋移廣東，以募兵事未竟，仍留貴州。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Guangdong, but because recruitment was unfinished he remained in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Guangdong, but because the recruitment drive was unfinished he stayed on in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 貴州產鉛，歲採運供鑄錢，以糧道主其事。

translations.literal: Guizhou produces lead, mined and transported annually to supply coinage; the grain intendant supervises the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou produces lead that is mined and shipped each year for minting, under the supervision of the grain intendant.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，良卿疏劾威寧知州劉標運鉛不如額，並虧工本運值，奪標職，令良卿詳讞。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year Liang Qing memorialized impeaching Weining Prefect Liu Biao for shipping less lead than the quota and also for deficits in operating capital and transport costs; Biao was stripped of office and Liang Qing was ordered to try the case in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year Liang Qing impeached Weining Prefect Liu Biao for falling short on lead shipments and for deficits in operating and transport costs; Biao was dismissed and Liang Qing was ordered to hear the case fully.

sentences.zh: 良卿疏陳標虧項，並劾糧道永泰，請簡大臣會鞫，上為遣內閣學士富察善如貴州會良卿按治。

translations.literal: Liang Qing memorialized Biao's deficits and also impeached Grain Intendant Yongtai, requesting a senior minister to join the interrogation; the Emperor sent Grand Secretariat Academician Fucha Shan to Guizhou to investigate jointly with Liang Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qing reported Biao's deficits and also impeached Grain Intendant Yongtai, asking that a senior minister join the inquiry; the Emperor dispatched Grand Secretariat Academician Fucha Shan to Guizhou to investigate with Liang Qing.

sentences.zh: 永泰揭戶部陳標虧項由長官婪索，因及良卿及按察使高積貪黷狀，上解良卿職，復命刑部侍郎錢維城、湖廣總督吳達善即訊。

translations.literal: Yongtai petitioned the Board of Revenue stating that Biao's deficits arose from superiors' greedy extortion, thereby implicating Liang Qing and Surveillance Commissioner Gao Ji in corruption; the Emperor relieved Liang Qing of office and again ordered Vice Minister of Justice Qian Weicheng and Huguang Governor-General Wu Dashan to interrogate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Yongtai appealed to the Board of Revenue, arguing that Biao's deficits came from extortion by his superiors and implicating Liang Qing and Surveillance Commissioner Gao Ji in corruption; the Emperor removed Liang Qing from office and ordered Vice Minister Qian Weicheng and Huguang Governor-General Wu Dashan to investigate immediately.

sentences.zh: 故事，奏摺置黃木匣，外護以黃綾袱，至御前始啟。

translations.literal: By precedent, memorials were placed in yellow wooden boxes wrapped in yellow silk pouches and opened only before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, memorials were sealed in yellow wooden boxes wrapped in yellow silk and opened only in the Emperor's presence.

sentences.zh: 上發副將軍阿桂軍中奏，於袱內得普安民吳倎訴官吏、土目私派累民狀，命吳達善密勘；

translations.literal: When the Emperor opened a duplicate of General Agui's report from the field, within the pouch he found a petition from Pu'an commoner Wu Tian accusing officials and native chieftains of unauthorized levies burdening the people; he ordered Wu Dashan to investigate secretly;
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor opened a duplicate of General Agui's field report, he found inside the wrapping a petition from Wu Tian, a commoner of Pu'an, accusing officials and native chieftains of illegal levies that oppressed the people; he ordered Wu Dashan to investigate in secret;

sentences.zh: 而劉標亦遣人詣戶部訴上官婪索，呈簿記，上申命吳達善嚴鞫。

translations.literal: Liu Biao also sent someone to the Board of Revenue accusing superiors of greedy extortion and presenting account books; the Emperor again ordered Wu Dashan to interrogate strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao also sent an agent to the Board of Revenue accusing his superiors of extortion and submitting account books; the Emperor again ordered Wu Dashan to conduct a rigorous inquiry.

sentences.zh: 吳達善先後疏言標積年虧帑至二十四萬有奇。

translations.literal: Wu Dashan successively memorialized that Biao's accumulated treasury deficits over the years exceeded two hundred and forty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Dashan reported in successive memorials that Biao's accumulated treasury shortfalls over the years exceeded two hundred and forty thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 良卿意在彌補掩覆，見事不可掩，乃以訪聞奏劾；

translations.literal: Liang Qing's intent was to cover up and conceal; when he saw the matter could no longer be hidden, only then did he memorialize an impeachment on the basis of hearsay;
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qing had meant to cover the matter up; when concealment became impossible, he impeached Biao only on the basis of what he claimed to have heard;

sentences.zh: 及追繳銀六千有奇，令留抵私填公項，不入查封，始終隱飾。

translations.literal: When more than six thousand taels were recovered, he ordered them retained to offset privately filled public accounts, not included in sealed assets—concealing throughout.
translations.idiomatic: When more than six thousand taels were recovered, he had them kept back to cover sums he had privately used to fill public accounts, excluding them from the sealed inventory—he concealed the truth from start to finish.

sentences.zh: 又及高積鬻儲庫水銀，良卿有袒庇狀。

translations.literal: The case also involved Gao Ji selling reserve treasury quicksilver; Liang Qing showed signs of shielding him.
translations.idiomatic: The inquiry also uncovered Gao Ji's sale of quicksilver from the reserve treasury, and Liang Qing had plainly shielded him.

sentences.zh: 良卿長支養廉，為前布政使張逢堯及積署布政使時支放。

translations.literal: Liang Qing had long drawn on integrity stipends, disbursed during former Financial Commissioner Zhang Fengyao's term and during Ji's acting service as financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Qing had long been drawing integrity stipends in advance, paid out during former Financial Commissioner Zhang Fengyao's term and during Ji's acting tenure.

sentences.zh: 普安州民吳國治訴知州陳昶籍軍興私派累民，良卿即令昶會鞫，不竟其事，乃致倎賄驛吏附奏事達御前。

translations.literal: Pu'an Prefecture commoner Wu Guozhi sued Prefect Chen Chang for unauthorized levies under the pretext of military levies burdening the people; Liang Qing had Chang conduct a joint interrogation but did not see the matter through, which led Tian to bribe a relay clerk and attach a petition that reached the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Guozhi, a commoner of Pu'an Prefecture, sued Prefect Chen Chang for illegal levies disguised as war expenses; Liang Qing had Chang hold a joint hearing but never finished the case, which allowed Tian to bribe a relay clerk and smuggle a petition through to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上乃責良卿負恩欺罔，罪不止於骫法婪贓，命即貴州省城處斬，銷旗籍，以其子富多、富永發伊犁，畀厄魯特為奴。

translations.literal: The Emperor then condemned Liang Qing for ingratitude and deception, his crime extending beyond bending the law and greedy bribery; he ordered immediate execution at the Guizhou provincial capital, annulment of banner registration, and that his sons Fuduo and Fuyong be sent to Ili and given as slaves to the Oirats.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor then denounced Liang Qing for betraying imperial favor and deceiving the throne, his guilt going beyond corruption and bribery; he ordered him executed at once in the Guizhou provincial capital, struck from the banner rolls, and his sons Fuduo and Fuyong sent to Ili as slaves to the Oirats.

sentences.zh: 積、逢堯、標皆坐譴。

translations.literal: Ji, Fengyao, and Biao were all punished.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, Fengyao, and Biao were all punished as well.

sentences.zh: 方世俊，字毓川，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Fang Shijun, courtesy name Yuchuan, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Shijun, styled Yuchuan, was from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四年進士，授戶部主事。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Qianlong, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 4, he entered the Board of Revenue as a principal clerk.

sentences.zh: 累遷太僕寺少卿，外授陝西布政使。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and posted outside as Financial Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud and was then posted as Financial Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，擢貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted to Governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he was made Governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，調湖南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year he was transferred to Governor of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year he was transferred to Governor of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 劉標訐發上官婪索，言世俊得銀六千有奇，上命奪官，逮送貴州，其僕承世俊得銀千。

translations.literal: Liu Biao denounced his superiors for greedy extortion, saying Shijun had received more than six thousand taels of silver; the Emperor ordered him stripped of rank and sent to Guizhou for trial, and his servant confirmed Shijun had received one thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao exposed his superiors' extortion, claiming Shijun had taken more than six thousand taels; the Emperor stripped him of rank and sent him to Guizhou for trial, and his servant admitted Shijun had received one thousand taels.

sentences.zh: 獄成，械致刑部，論絞決，上命改監候。

translations.literal: When the case was concluded, he was shackled and sent to the Ministry of Justice; sentenced to strangulation, the Emperor ordered commutation to imprisonment awaiting execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the trial concluded he was sent in chains to the Ministry of Justice and sentenced to strangulation; the Emperor commuted the sentence to imprisonment awaiting execution.

sentences.zh: 秋讞入情實，伏法。

translations.literal: At the autumn judicial review the case was entered as genuine, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At the autumn review the case was confirmed as capital, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 錢度，字希裴，江南武進人。

translations.literal: Qian Du, courtesy name Xipei, was a native of Wujin in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Du, styled Xipei, was from Wujin in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年進士，授吏部主事，累遷廣西道監察御史。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the first year of Qianlong, he was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and cumulatively promoted to censor of the Guangxi Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 1, he entered the Ministry of Personnel as a principal clerk and rose to censor of the Guangxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 外授安徽徽州知府，累擢至方面。

translations.literal: Posted outside as Prefect of Huizhou in Anhui, he was cumulatively promoted to provincial commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: Posted out as Prefect of Huizhou in Anhui, he worked his way up to provincial commissioner rank.

sentences.zh: 其為江安督糧道、河庫道，皆再任，歷十餘年。

translations.literal: His service as grain transport commissioner of Jiang'an and as river treasury commissioner were both held twice, spanning more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He served twice each as grain transport commissioner of Jiang'an and as river treasury commissioner, for more than ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其久任奮勉。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his long service and diligent effort.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended his long tenure and steady diligence.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，授雲南布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was appointed Financial Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he became Financial Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，遷廣東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he was transferred to Governor of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he was made Governor of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 師方徵緬甸，度主餽軍，命以巡撫銜領布政使。

translations.literal: The army was then campaigning against Burma; Du managed military supplies and was ordered to hold governor's rank while leading as financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: While the army was campaigning in Burma, Du oversaw military supplies and was ordered to serve as financial commissioner with governor's rank.

sentences.zh: 未歲，移廣西巡撫，乃之官，賀縣囚越獄，度請寬知縣鄭之翀罪。

translations.literal: Before the year was out he was transferred to Governor of Guangxi; upon taking office, prisoners escaped in Hexian County, and Du asked leniency for Magistrate Zheng Zhichong.
translations.idiomatic: Before the year ended he was transferred to Governor of Guangxi; soon after he took office prisoners broke jail in Hexian County, and Du asked that Magistrate Zheng Zhichong be treated leniently.

sentences.zh: 上命奪之翀職，責度寬縱。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhichong stripped of office and rebuked Du for excessive leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor dismissed Zhichong and censured Du for being too lenient.

sentences.zh: 學政梅立本按試鬱林，索供應，民聚閧。

translations.literal: Education Intendant Mei Liben, while conducting examinations at Yulin, demanded supplies, and the people gathered in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Education Intendant Mei Liben, conducting examinations at Yulin, demanded provisions from the locals, and the people rose in protest.

sentences.zh: 上命度定學政供應夫船事例，度擬從寬備，失上指，仍左授雲南布政使。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Du to set regulations for education intendant supplies and boat services; Du drafted lenient provisions, missed the Emperor's intent, and was demoted back to Financial Commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Du to establish rules for the supplies and transport owed to education intendants; Du drafted overly lenient regulations, missed the Emperor's intent, and was demoted to Financial Commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，監銅廠。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year he supervised the copper mines.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-seventh year he was put in charge of the copper mines.

sentences.zh: 宜良知縣硃一深揭戶部，告度貪婪，勒屬吏市金玉，上命刑部侍郎袁守侗如雲南會總督彰寶、巡撫李湖按治。

translations.literal: Yiliang Magistrate Zhu Yishen petitioned the Board of Revenue accusing Du of greed and forcing subordinate officials to procure gold and jade; the Emperor ordered Vice Minister of Justice Yuan Shoutong to go to Yunnan to investigate jointly with Governor-General Zhang Bao and Governor Li Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Yiliang Magistrate Zhu Yishen appealed to the Board of Revenue, accusing Du of greed and coercing subordinates into supplying gold and jade; the Emperor sent Vice Minister Yuan Shoutong to Yunnan to investigate with Governor-General Zhang Bao and Governor Li Hu.

sentences.zh: 貴州巡撫圖思德奏獲度僕持金玉諸器，自京師將往雲南，值銀五千以上；

translations.literal: Guizhou Governor Tuside memorialized that Du's servant had been seized carrying gold, jade, and various vessels from the capital bound for Yunnan, worth more than five thousand taels of silver;
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Governor Tuside reported that Du's servant had been caught carrying gold, jade, and other valuables from the capital toward Yunnan, worth more than five thousand taels;

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫海明奏獲度僕攜銀二萬九千有奇，自雲南將往江南，並得度寄子酆書，令為複壁藏金，為永久計；

translations.literal: Jiangxi Governor Haiming memorialized that Du's servant had been seized carrying more than twenty-nine thousand taels of silver from Yunnan bound for Jiangnan, and a letter from Du to his son Feng instructing him to build hidden compartments to store gold as a permanent plan;
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Governor Haiming reported that another of Du's servants had been caught with more than twenty-nine thousand taels en route from Yunnan to Jiangnan, along with a letter from Du to his son Feng instructing him to build secret compartments for gold as a long-term hoard;

sentences.zh: 兩江總督高晉籍度家，得窖藏銀二萬七千，又寄頓金二千。

translations.literal: Liangjiang Governor-General Gao Jin searched Du's home and found buried silver totaling twenty-seven thousand taels, plus deposited gold of two thousand taels.
translations.idiomatic: Liangjiang Governor-General Gao Jin searched Du's household and uncovered twenty-seven thousand taels of buried silver and two thousand taels of stored gold.

sentences.zh: 守侗等訊得度刻扣銅本平餘，及勒屬吏市金玉得值，具服，逮送京師。

translations.literal: Shoutong and the others interrogated and found that Du had systematically deducted copper capital surpluses and coerced subordinate officials to procure gold and jade for their value; he fully confessed and was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shoutong and his colleagues established that Du had routinely skimmed copper-fund surpluses and forced subordinates to supply gold and jade; he confessed fully and was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 命軍機大臣會刑部覆讞，以度侵欺勒索贓私具實，罪當斬，命即行法。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Grand Council ministers together with the Ministry of Justice to review the case; Du's embezzlement, extortion, and private gain were fully verified, the crime warranting decapitation, and he was ordered executed immediately.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Council ministers and the Ministry of Justice reviewed the case, confirmed Du's embezzlement and extortion, found the capital offense proved, and he was executed at once.

sentences.zh: 子酆亦論絞，上為改緩決。

translations.literal: His son Feng was also sentenced to strangulation; the Emperor changed it to delayed execution.
translations.idiomatic: His son Feng was also sentenced to strangulation, but the Emperor commuted it to delayed execution.

sentences.zh: 尋遇赦，仍不令應試出仕。

translations.literal: Soon afterward an amnesty was granted, but he was still barred from taking examinations or entering office.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty followed, but he remained barred from the examinations and from office.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶五年，弛其禁。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiaqing the prohibition was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 5 the ban was lifted.

sentences.zh: 覺羅伍拉納，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Wulana, of the Aisin Gioro clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana, of the Aisin Gioro clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain Yellow.

sentences.zh: 初授戶部筆帖式，外除張家口理事同知，累遷福建布政使。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a bithesi clerk in the Board of Revenue, then posted outside as sub-prefect of Zhangjiakou, and cumulatively promoted to Financial Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a bithesi clerk in the Board of Revenue, was posted out as sub-prefect of Zhangjiakou, and rose to Financial Commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 林爽文之亂，伍拉納主餽軍，往來蚶江、廈門，事定，賜花翎，遷河南巡撫。

translations.literal: During Lin Shuangwen's rebellion, Wulana managed military supplies, traveling between Hanjiang and Xiamen; when the affair was settled he was granted a peacock feather and promoted to Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During Lin Shuangwen's rebellion Wulana oversaw military supplies, shuttling between Hanjiang and Xiamen; when order was restored he received a peacock feather and was made Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 乾隆五十四年，授閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year of Qianlong he was appointed Governor-General of Min-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 54 he was appointed Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 上以福建民情獷悍，戒伍拉納當與巡撫徐嗣曾商榷整飭。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering the people of Fujian fierce and unruly, admonished Wulana that he must consult with Governor Xu Sizeng on measures of reform and discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the people of Fujian fierce and hard to govern, the Emperor warned Wulana to work closely with Governor Xu Sizeng on restoring order.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納督屬吏捕盜，先後所誅殺百數十人。

translations.literal: Wulana supervised subordinate officials in capturing bandits; in succession more than a hundred were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana put his subordinates to hunting bandits and, over time, had more than a hundred put to death.

sentences.zh: 以內地民多渡海至台灣，疏請海口設官渡，便稽察。

translations.literal: Because many inland people crossed the sea to Taiwan, he memorialized requesting that official ferry crossings be established at seaports to facilitate inspection.
translations.idiomatic: As many inland residents were crossing to Taiwan, he memorialized asking that official ferry stations be set up at harbors to ease inspection.

sentences.zh: 時定往台灣者出蚶江，民舟或自廈門渡，亦令至蚶江報驗，疏請罷其例，俾得迳出廈門。

translations.literal: At that time those bound for Taiwan were required to depart from Hanjiang, yet civilian boats sometimes crossed from Xiamen and were also ordered to go to Hanjiang for inspection; he memorialized requesting that this rule be abolished so they might depart directly from Xiamen.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers to Taiwan were then required to leave from Hanjiang; even boats sailing from Xiamen had to report there for inspection. He asked that this rule be dropped so they could embark directly from Xiamen.

sentences.zh: 言者以海中島嶼多，流民散處為盜藪，當毀其廬，徙其民，毋使滋蔓。

translations.literal: Memorializers held that because there were many islands in the sea where displaced people were scattered as nests of bandits, their dwellings should be destroyed, the people relocated, and their spread not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that the many offshore islands where refugees had settled had become thieves' lairs, and that their dwellings should be destroyed and the inhabitants relocated before the trouble spread.

sentences.zh: 下濱海諸直省議，伍拉納疏言：「福建海中諸島嶼，流民散處，凡已編甲輸糧者，當不在例中。」

translations.literal: The matter was referred to the coastal provinces for deliberation; Wulana memorialized: "Among the islands in the Fujian seas where displaced people are scattered, all who have been registered in household rolls and pay grain taxes should be excluded from this measure."
translations.idiomatic: The coastal provinces were consulted. Wulana memorialized: "On the Fujian islands where refugees live scattered, anyone already registered and paying grain taxes should not be covered by this policy."

sentences.zh: 上命諸島嶼非例當封禁，皆任其居處。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered that all islands that under precedent ought not to be sealed and forbidden should be left to their inhabitants to dwell as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ruled that islands not subject to closure under existing rules should remain open to settlement.

sentences.zh: 浙江嘉善縣民訴縣吏徵漕浮收，下伍拉納按治，論如律。

translations.literal: People of Jiashan County in Zhejiang complained that county officials had over-collected grain transport levies; the case was referred to Wulana for investigation, and sentence was passed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When residents of Jiashan County in Zhejiang accused county officials of overcharging on grain transport levies, the case was sent to Wulana; he investigated and punished them under the statutes.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納治尚嚴，疏劾金門鎮總兵羅英笈巡洋兵船遇盜不以實報，英笈坐譴；

translations.literal: Wulana's governance tended toward severity; he memorialized impeaching Luo Yingji, regional commander at Jinmen Fort, for not reporting truthfully when patrol boats encountered bandits, and Yingji was punished;
translations.idiomatic: Wulana ran a strict administration. He impeached Luo Yingji, garrison commander at Jinmen, for filing false reports when patrol boats met bandits; Yingji was punished;

sentences.zh: 又論邵武營守備餘朝武等侵餉，營吏黃國材等冒餉，黃岩右營守備葉起發屬兵遇盜不以實報，外委陳學明避盜偽為被創，營兵柯大斌誣告營官，皆傅重比。

translations.literal: He also sentenced Yu Chaowu, garrison commander of Shaowu Camp, and others for embezzling pay; camp clerk Huang Guocai and others for falsely claiming pay; Ye Qifa, garrison commander of the Right Battalion at Huangyan, for his subordinates not reporting truthfully when encountering bandits; outer deputy Chen Xueming for feigning wounds to avoid bandits; and camp soldier Ke Dabing for falsely accusing his officer—all were sentenced under aggravated statutes.
translations.idiomatic: He also convicted Yu Chaowu, garrison commander of Shaowu Camp, and others of embezzling pay; Huang Guocai and other camp clerks of drawing false salaries; Ye Qifa, garrison commander of the Right Battalion at Huangyan, because his men had lied about encounters with bandits; outer deputy Chen Xueming of faking wounds to avoid fighting; and camp soldier Ke Dabing of falsely accusing his officer—all under aggravated penalties.

sentences.zh: 五十七年，同安民陳蘇老、晉江民陳滋等為亂，設靝雰會。

translations.literal: In the fifty-seventh year, Chen Sulao of Tong'an, Chen Zi of Jinjiang, and others rose in rebellion and established the Tian Fen Society.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-seventh year Chen Sulao of Tong'an, Chen Zi of Jinjiang, and others rebelled and formed the Tian Fen Society.

sentences.zh: 「《表氣》雰」字妄造，以代「天地」。

translations.literal: The spurious graph cluster biaoqi fen in the title Biaoqi Fen was arbitrarily invented to replace "Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: They invented a bogus written form, biaoqi fen, to stand in for the words Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納率按察使戚蓼生赴泉州捕得蘇老等，誅一百五十八人，戍六十九人。

translations.literal: Wulana led Surveillance Commissioner Qi Liaosheng to Quanzhou, captured Sulao and the others, executed one hundred fifty-eight people, and banished sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana took Surveillance Commissioner Qi Liaosheng to Quanzhou, captured Sulao and his followers, executed 158, and banished 69.

sentences.zh: 五十九年，義烏民何世來，宣平民王元、樓德新等為亂，立邪教。

translations.literal: In the fifty-ninth year, He Shilai of Yiwu, Wang Yuan and Lou Dexin of Xuanping, and others rose in rebellion and established a heterodox sect.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-ninth year He Shilai of Yiwu, Wang Yuan and Lou Dexin of Xuanping, and others rebelled and founded a heterodox sect.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納率按察使錢受椿赴金華。

translations.literal: Wulana led Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun to Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana went to Jinhua with Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫吉慶已捕誅世來、德新，伍拉納覆讞諸脅從，复誅鮑茂山、吳阿成等，還福建至浦城，捕得元，誅之。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Ji Qing had already captured and executed Shilai and Dexin; Wulana re-tried the coerced followers, again executed Bao Maoshan, Wu Acheng, and others, returned to Fujian, and at Pucheng captured Yuan and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Ji Qing had already captured and executed Shilai and Dexin. Wulana re-tried the coerced followers, put Bao Maoshan, Wu Acheng, and others to death, then returned to Fujian; at Pucheng he captured Yuan and executed him.

sentences.zh: 六十年，台灣盜陳周全為亂，陷彰化。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year, the Taiwan bandit Chen Quanzhou rebelled and took Changhua.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixtieth year the Taiwan bandit Chen Quanzhou rebelled and seized Changhua.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納出駐泉州，發兵令署陸路提督烏蘭保、海壇鎮總兵特克什布赴剿，彰化民楊仲舍等擊破周全，亂已定。

translations.literal: Wulana went out to station at Quanzhou, dispatched troops, and ordered Acting Provincial Infantry Commander Ulanbao and Haitan garrison commander Tekeshibu to suppress them; Yang Zhongshe and others in Changhua defeated Quanzhou, and the rebellion was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana moved his headquarters to Quanzhou, sent troops, and ordered Acting Provincial Infantry Commander Ulanbao and Haitan garrison commander Tekeshibu to suppress the rebels; Yang Zhongshe and others in Changhua routed Quanzhou, and the rebellion was put down.

sentences.zh: 是歲，漳、泉被水，飢。

translations.literal: That year Zhangzhou and Quanzhou were flooded and suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhangzhou and Quanzhou were flooded, and the people went hungry.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納至，民閧集乞賑，未以聞。

translations.literal: When Wulana arrived, the people gathered in crowds begging for relief, but he did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Wulana arrived, crowds of people begged for relief, yet he never reported it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上促伍拉納赴台灣，累詔詰責，伍拉納自泉州往。

translations.literal: The Emperor urged Wulana to go to Taiwan, repeatedly issuing edicts of censure; Wulana set out from Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor pressed Wulana to go to Taiwan, censuring him again and again in edict after edict; Wulana finally set out from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 福州將軍魁倫疏言：「伍拉納性急，按察使錢受椿等迎合，治獄多未協。

translations.literal: Fuzhou General Kuilun memorialized: "Wulana is impatient in temperament; Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun and others flatter him; many of his adjudications are improper.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhou General Kuilun memorialized: "Wulana is hot-tempered; Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun and others indulge him, and many of his legal judgments are unsound.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉被水，米值昂，民貧，巡撫浦霖等不為之所，多入海為盜。

translations.literal: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou were flooded; rice prices rose; the people were impoverished; Governor Pu Lin and others did nothing for them, and many took to the sea as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangzhou and Quanzhou had been flooded; rice prices soared and the people were destitute, yet Governor Pu Lin and others did nothing for them, and many turned to piracy.

sentences.zh: 虎門近在省會，亦有盜舟出沒。」

translations.literal: Humen is close to the provincial capital, yet bandit boats also appear there."
translations.idiomatic: Humen lies near the provincial capital, yet even there bandit boats were appearing."

sentences.zh: 上為罷伍拉納、浦霖，命兩廣總督覺羅長麟署總督，魁倫署巡撫。

translations.literal: The Emperor dismissed Wulana and Pu Lin, ordered Liangguang Governor-General Aisin Gioro Changlin to act as governor-general, and Kuilun to act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor removed Wulana and Pu Lin from office, ordered Liangguang Governor-General Aisin Gioro Changlin to serve as acting governor-general, and Kuilun as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納至台灣，劾鹿仔港巡檢硃繼功以喪去官，賊起，即攜眷內渡，請奪官戍新疆。

translations.literal: When Wulana reached Taiwan, he impeached Luzai Harbor sub-inspector Zhu Jigong for leaving office on mourning leave; when bandits rose Jigong immediately took his family across to the mainland, and Wulana asked that Jigong be stripped of office and banished to Xinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wulana reached Taiwan, he impeached Luzai Harbor sub-inspector Zhu Jigong, who had left office to mourn a parent's death; when the rebels rose Jigong at once took his family back to the mainland, and Wulana asked that he be stripped of rank and exiled to Xinjiang.

sentences.zh: 上諭曰：「伍拉納為總督，台灣賊起，陷城戕官，朕屢旨嚴飭始行，繼功丁憂巡檢，轉責其攜眷內渡，加以遠戍。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued an edict: "Wulana as governor-general—when bandits rose in Taiwan, cities fell and officials were killed, and I repeatedly issued strict orders before he would act; Jigong is a sub-inspector in mourning, yet Wulana instead blames him for taking his family across the strait and would banish him to distant service.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said: "Wulana was governor-general. When rebels rose in Taiwan, cities fell and officials were slaughtered, and I had to issue repeated stern orders before he would move. Jigong is a sub-inspector in mourning, yet Wulana turns on him for taking his family back across the strait and would send him into distant exile.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納畏葸遷延，乃欲以此自掩，何其不知恥也！」

translations.literal: Wulana was fearful and dilatory, and now seeks to cover himself with this—how utterly shameless!"
translations.idiomatic: Wulana was timid and slow to act, and now he would cover himself with this—what shamelessness!"

sentences.zh: 伍拉納、浦霖貪縱、婪索諸屬吏，州縣倉庫多虧缺。

translations.literal: Wulana and Pu Lin were greedy and indulgent, extorting their subordinate officials; prefecture and county granaries showed many shortfalls.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana and Pu Lin were greedy and lax, extorting their subordinates, and granaries in the prefectures and counties showed widespread shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 伍拉納嘗疏陳清查諸州縣倉庫，虧穀六十四萬有奇、銀三十六萬有奇，限三年責諸主者償納。

translations.literal: Wulana had once memorialized reporting an audit of prefecture and county granaries: grain shortfalls of more than six hundred forty thousand and silver of more than three hundred sixty thousand taels, giving three years for the responsible officials to make restitution.
translations.idiomatic: Wulana had once memorialized on an audit of prefectural and county granaries, reporting grain shortfalls of more than 640,000 and silver shortfalls of more than 360,000 taels, and giving the responsible officials three years to make restitution.

sentences.zh: 至是，魁倫疏論諸州縣倉庫虧缺，伍拉納所奏非實數。

translations.literal: At this point Kuilun memorialized on granary shortfalls in the prefectures and counties, holding that Wulana's reported figures were not the true amounts.
translations.idiomatic: By then Kuilun had memorialized on granary shortfalls in the prefectures and counties, arguing that the figures Wulana had reported were not the true totals.

sentences.zh: 上命伍拉納、浦霖及布政使伊轍布、按察使錢受椿皆奪官，交長麟、魁倫按讞。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Wulana, Pu Lin, Financial Commissioner Yizhebu, and Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun all stripped of office and handed over to Changlin and Kuilun to investigate and judge.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor stripped Wulana, Pu Lin, Financial Commissioner Yizhebu, and Surveillance Commissioner Qian Shouchun of their posts and handed them over to Changlin and Kuilun for investigation and trial.

sentences.zh: 長麟、魁倫勘布政司庫吏周經侵庫帑八萬有奇，具獄辭以上。

translations.literal: Changlin and Kuilun investigated Zhou Jing, a clerk in the provincial financial commissioner's treasury, for embezzling more than eighty thousand taels from the treasury, and submitted a full case report.
translations.idiomatic: Changlin and Kuilun investigated Zhou Jing, a clerk in the provincial treasurer's office, for embezzling more than 80,000 taels from the treasury and submitted a complete case report.

sentences.zh: 上疑長麟等意將歸獄於經，斥其徇隱。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected Changlin and the others intended to lay all guilt on Zhou Jing and rebuked them for shielding others.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor suspected that Changlin and his colleagues meant to pin the whole case on Zhou Jing and rebuked them for shielding the guilty.

sentences.zh: 長麟等疏發伍拉納受鹽商賕十五萬，霖亦受二萬，別疏發受椿讞長秦械鬥獄，獄斃至十人，得賕銷案。

translations.literal: Changlin and the others memorialized exposing that Wulana had taken one hundred fifty thousand taels in bribes from salt merchants and Lin had taken twenty thousand; in a separate memorial they exposed that Shouchun, in judging a Chang-Qin affray case, had ten die in custody and had taken bribes to quash the case.
translations.idiomatic: Changlin and his colleagues then memorialized that Wulana had taken 150,000 taels in bribes from salt merchants and Lin 20,000; in another memorial they exposed that Shouchun, while judging a Chang-Qin brawl case in which ten men died in custody, had taken bribes to suppress the case.

sentences.zh: 籍伍拉納家，得銀四十萬有奇、如意至一百餘柄，上比之元載胡椒八百斛；

translations.literal: Wulana's household was inventoried: more than four hundred thousand taels of silver and more than a hundred ruyi scepters; the Emperor compared this to Yuan Zai's eight hundred piculs of pepper;
translations.idiomatic: An inventory of Wulana's household turned up more than 400,000 taels of silver and more than a hundred ruyi scepters; the Emperor compared the hoard to Yuan Zai's eight hundred piculs of pepper;

sentences.zh: 籍霖家，得窖藏金七百、銀二十八萬，田舍值六萬有奇，他服物稱是；

translations.literal: Lin's household was inventoried: seven hundred taels of buried gold, two hundred eighty thousand taels of silver, fields and buildings worth more than sixty thousand, and personal goods in proportion;
translations.idiomatic: An inventory of Lin's household found seven hundred taels of buried gold, 280,000 taels of silver, fields and buildings worth more than 60,000, and personal goods to match;

sentences.zh: 逮京師，廷鞫服罪，命立斬。

translations.literal: They were brought to the capital, tried at court, confessed, and ordered immediately executed.
translations.idiomatic: They were brought to the capital, tried before the court, confessed, and were ordered executed at once.

sentences.zh: 伊轍布亦逮京師，道死。

translations.literal: Yizhebu was also brought to the capital but died en route.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhebu was also sent to the capital but died on the way.

sentences.zh: 受椿監送還福建，夾二次，重笞四十，乃集在省諸官吏處斬；

translations.literal: Shouchun was escorted back to Fujian under guard, subjected twice to the leg-press torture and forty blows of heavy bamboo, then executed before the assembled provincial officials;
translations.idiomatic: Shouchun was escorted back to Fujian under guard, put twice to the leg-press and given forty strokes of heavy bamboo, then executed before the assembled provincial officials;

sentences.zh: 又以長麟主寬貸，奪官召還，以魁倫代之，遂興大獄，諸州縣虧帑一萬以上皆斬，誅李堂等十人，餘譴黜有差。

translations.literal: Because Changlin had advocated leniency, he was stripped of office and recalled; Kuilun replaced him, and a great prosecution followed—all officials with treasury shortfalls above ten thousand taels were executed; Li Tang and nine others were put to death; the rest were punished or dismissed according to degree.
translations.idiomatic: Because Changlin had favored leniency, he was stripped of rank and recalled; Kuilun replaced him, and a sweeping prosecution followed—every official with treasury shortfalls above 10,000 taels was executed; Li Tang and nine others were put to death; the rest were punished or dismissed in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 霖，浙江嘉善人。

translations.literal: Lin was a native of Jiashan in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was a native of Jiashan in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 乾隆三十一年進士，授戶部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the thirty-first year of Qianlong, he was appointed a secretary in the Board of Revenue and was promoted twice to director.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of Qianlong 31, he was appointed a secretary in the Board of Revenue and was promoted twice to director.

sentences.zh: 外授湖北安襄鄖道。

translations.literal: He was posted outside the capital as intendant of An-Xiang-Yun Circuit in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as intendant of An-Xiang-Yun Circuit in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 累遷福建巡撫，移湖南，复遷福建。

translations.literal: He rose cumulatively to Governor of Fujian, was transferred to Hunan, then was transferred back to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Governor of Fujian, was transferred to Hunan, and then was transferred back to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 及得罪，上謂：「伍拉納未嘗學問，或不知潔己奉公之義。

translations.literal: When they fell from grace, the Emperor said: "Wulana never had scholarly training and may not have known the meaning of keeping himself clean and serving the public.
translations.idiomatic: When they were condemned, the Emperor said: "Wulana never had a scholar's training and may not have understood what it means to keep oneself clean and serve the public.

sentences.zh: 霖以科目進，起自寒素，擢任封疆，乃貪黷無厭，罔顧廉恥，尚得謂有人心者乎？」

translations.literal: Lin entered through the examination system, rose from humble origins, and was elevated to a frontier post—yet he was insatiably corrupt, heedless of integrity and shame. Can such a man still be called human?"
translations.idiomatic: Lin entered by the examination route, rose from humble origins, and was elevated to a frontier post—yet he was insatiably corrupt and heedless of integrity and shame. Can such a man still be called human?"

sentences.zh: 霖及伍拉納、伊轍布、受椿諸子皆用王亶望例戍伊犁。

translations.literal: The sons of Lin, Wulana, Yizhebu, and Shouchun were all exiled to Ili under the Wang Danwang precedent.
translations.idiomatic: The sons of Lin, Wulana, Yizhebu, and Shouchun were all exiled to Ili under the precedent set in the Wang Danwang case.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，赦還。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing they were pardoned and allowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 4 they were pardoned and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 論曰：高宗譴諸貪吏，身大辟，家籍沒，僇及於子孫。

translations.literal: Commentary: Gaozong punished corrupt officials severely—they themselves suffered capital punishment, their households were confiscated, and disgrace extended to their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Gaozong punished corrupt officials with the utmost severity—they themselves were executed, their households were confiscated, and disgrace reached their descendants.

sentences.zh: 凡所連染，窮治不稍貸，可謂嚴矣！

translations.literal: All who were implicated were pursued to the end without the slightest leniency—truly stern!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone implicated was pursued to the end without mercy—truly stern!

sentences.zh: 乃營私骫法，前後相望，豈以執政者尚貪侈，源濁流不能清歟？

translations.literal: Yet private gain and bending of the law followed one upon another—was it because those in power remained greedy and extravagant, so that when the source is turbid the stream cannot run clear?
translations.idiomatic: Yet private gain and bending of the law went on one after another—was it because those in power were still greedy and extravagant, so that when the source is muddy the stream cannot run clear?

sentences.zh: 抑以坐苞苴敗者，亦或論才宥罪，執法未嘗無撓歟？

translations.literal: Or when men fell through bribery, was talent sometimes invoked to mitigate guilt—so that law enforcement was not always unbending?
translations.idiomatic: Or when men fell through bribery, was talent sometimes invoked to win pardon—so that enforcement was not always without compromise?

sentences.zh: 然觀其所誅殛，要可以鑑矣！

translations.literal: Yet seen by those they executed and destroyed, the lesson should suffice as a warning!
translations.idiomatic: Yet judged by those they executed and ruined, the lesson should be warning enough!
